description: Sequential quadratic programming with variable bounds and general nonlinear constraints.
source:
module playground_psqp_functions
   use psqp_module, only: psqp_class,wp => psqp_wp
   implicit none
contains
    subroutine obj(me,nf,x,ff)

        !! user supplied subroutine (calculation of ff)

        class(psqp_class),intent(inout) :: me
        real(wp) :: ff
        integer  :: nf
        real(wp) :: x(nf)

        ff = x(1)**2 + x(2)**2 + x(3)  !objective function

    end subroutine obj

    subroutine dobj(me,nf,x,gf)

        !! user supplied subroutine (calculation of gf)

        class(psqp_class),intent(inout) :: me
        integer  :: nf
        real(wp) :: gf(nf),x(nf)

        gf(1) = 2.0_wp*x(1)
        gf(2) = 2.0_wp*x(2)
        gf(3) = 1.0_wp

    end subroutine dobj

    subroutine con(me,nf,kc,x,fc)

        !! user supplied subroutine (calculation of fc)

        class(psqp_class),intent(inout) :: me
        real(wp) :: fc
        integer  :: kc,nf
        real(wp) :: x(nf)

        select case (kc)
        case(1)
            fc = x(1)*x(2) - x(3)       !equality constraint (==0)
        case(2)
            fc = x(3) - 1.0_wp          !inequality constraint (>=0)
        case default
            error stop 'invalid kc'
        end select

    end subroutine con

    subroutine dcon(me,nf,kc,x,gc)

        !! user supplied subroutine (calculation of gc)

        class(psqp_class),intent(inout) :: me
        integer  :: kc,nf
        real(wp) :: gc(nf),x(nf)

        select case (kc)
        case(1)
            gc(1) = x(2)
            gc(2) = x(1)
            gc(3) = -1.0_wp
        case(2)
            gc(1) = 0.0_wp
            gc(2) = 0.0_wp
            gc(3) = 1.0_wp
        case default
            error stop 'invalid kc'
        end select

    end subroutine dcon

end module

! Minimize x1**2+x2**2+x3 with x1*x2=x3 and x3>=1.
! The minimum is 3 at (1,1,1) or (-1,-1,1).
program demo_psqp
   use playground_psqp_functions
   use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   implicit none
   type(psqp_class) :: solver
   real(wp) :: x(3),xl(3),xu(3),cf(3),cl(2),cu(2),rpar(5),f,cmax,gmax
   integer :: ix(3),ic(2),ipar(6),status
   x = [1.0_wp,2.0_wp,3.0_wp]
   xl = -10; xu = 10; ix = 3
   ic = [5,1]; cl = 0; cu = 0
   ipar = [500,1000,0,0,1,1]
   rpar = [0.0_wp,1e-10_wp,1e-10_wp,1e-8_wp,0.0_wp]
   call solver%psqpn(3,1,2,x,ix,xl,xu,cf,ic,cl,cu,ipar,rpar,f,cmax,gmax,0,status,obj,dobj,con,dcon)
   if (status<=0) error stop 'Optimization failed'
   if (.not. all(ieee_is_finite(x))) error stop 'Nonfinite optimum'
   if (.not. ieee_is_finite(f)) error stop 'Nonfinite objective'
   if (maxval(abs(abs(x)-1.0_wp))>1e-5_wp .or. x(3)<0) error stop 'Known optimum differs'
   if (abs(x(1)*x(2)-x(3))>1e-7_wp .or. x(3)<1.0_wp-1e-7_wp) error stop 'Constraint violated'
   if (abs(f-3.0_wp)>1e-6_wp) error stop 'Wrong objective'
   print '(a,3f14.8)', 'Optimal variables: ',x
   print '(a,f14.8)', 'Minimum objective: ',f
   print '(a,es12.3)', 'Maximum constraint violation: ',cmax
   print '(a,i0)', 'Termination code: ',status
   print '(a)', 'PASS psqp'
end program

description: Constrained optimization designed for nearly linear problems with many constraints.
source:
module playground_optgra_functions
   use optgra_module, only: optgra,wp => optgra_wp
   implicit none
contains
   subroutine values(me,x,c,i)
      class(optgra), intent(inout) :: me
      real(wp), intent(in) :: x(:)
      real(wp), intent(out) :: c(:)
      integer, intent(in) :: i
      c(1) = sum(x)-3.0_wp
      c(2) = sum((x-1.0_wp)**2)
   end subroutine
   subroutine derivatives(me,x,c,jac)
      class(optgra), intent(inout) :: me
      real(wp), intent(in) :: x(:)
      real(wp), intent(out) :: c(:),jac(:,:)
      call values(me,x,c,0)
      jac(1,:) = 1
      jac(2,:) = 2*(x-1.0_wp)
   end subroutine
end module

program demo_optgra
   use playground_optgra_functions
   use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   implicit none
   type(optgra) :: solver
   real(wp) :: x(2),c(2)
   integer :: status,iterations,units(3),i
   character(len=80), parameter :: cnames(2)=[character(len=80) :: 'x+y-3','objective']
   character(len=80), parameter :: xnames(2)=[character(len=80) :: 'x','y']
   do i=1,3
      open(newunit=units(i),status='scratch',action='readwrite')
   end do
   ! Consca specifies convergence thresholds, not unit scale factors.
   call solver%initialize(2,1,values,derivatives,[1e-4_wp,1e-4_wp],[1,1],[1e-7_wp,1e-9_wp], &
      cnames,[5,9],[1,-1],1,[1e-5_wp,1e-5_wp],1.0_wp,1.0_wp,100,10,10,10,10, &
      units(1),0,0,[1.0_wp,1.0_wp],xnames,[1,1],[0,0],units(2),0,0,units(3),0,2)
   x = [0.0_wp,0.0_wp]
   call solver%solve(x,c,status,iterations)
   print '(a,i0)', 'Solver termination: ',status
   if (.not. all(ieee_is_finite(x))) error stop 'Nonfinite optimum'
   if (status /= 1) error stop 'Solver did not report a feasible optimum'
   if (maxval(abs(x-1.5_wp))>1e-5_wp) error stop 'Known optimum differs'
   if (sum(x)<3.0_wp-1e-7_wp) error stop 'Constraint violated'
   if (abs(sum((x-1.0_wp)**2)-0.5_wp)>1e-5_wp) error stop 'Wrong objective'
   print '(a)', 'Minimize (x-1)**2+(y-1)**2 subject to x+y >= 3.'
   print '(a,2f14.8)', 'Optimal x,y: ',x
   print '(a,f14.8)', 'Objective:   ',sum((x-1.0_wp)**2)
   print '(a,es12.3)', 'Constraint violation: ',max(0.0_wp,3.0_wp-sum(x))
   call solver%destroy()
   do i=1,3
      close(units(i))
   end do
   print '(a)', 'PASS optgra'
end program

description: Matrix inverses and singular-value-decomposition pseudoinverses.
source:
! A rank-one matrix needs an explicit singular-value cutoff in this API.
program demo_forinv
   use kinds, only: rk
   use forinv, only: inv
   use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   implicit none
   real(rk) :: a(3,2),workspace(3,2),pinv(2,3),b(3),x(2),left(3,3),right(2,2),errors(4)
   integer :: i
   a(:,1) = [1.0_rk,2.0_rk,3.0_rk]
   a(:,2) = 2*a(:,1)
   b = a(:,1)
   ! The pinned ForSVD passes its input to LAPACK workspace despite INTENT(IN).
   ! Preserve the original matrix explicitly for residuals and later use.
   workspace = a
   pinv = inv(workspace,tol=1e-10_rk)
   if (.not. all(ieee_is_finite(pinv))) error stop 'Nonfinite pseudoinverse'
   left = matmul(a,pinv); right = matmul(pinv,a)
   errors = [maxval(abs(matmul(left,a)-a)),maxval(abs(matmul(right,pinv)-pinv)), &
      maxval(abs(transpose(left)-left)),maxval(abs(transpose(right)-right))]
   if (any(errors>1e-11_rk)) error stop 'Moore-Penrose identities fail'
   x = matmul(pinv,b)
   ! All solutions satisfy x1+2*x2=1; the minimum-norm one is (1/5,2/5).
   if (maxval(abs(x-[0.2_rk,0.4_rk]))>1e-11_rk) error stop 'Wrong minimum-norm solution'
   if (maxval(abs(matmul(a,x)-b))>1e-11_rk) error stop 'Residual too large'
   print '(a)', 'Pseudoinverse of a rank-deficient 3 by 2 matrix:'
   do i=1,2
      print '(3f14.8)',pinv(i,:)
   end do
   print '(a,2f14.8)', 'Minimum-norm solution: ',x

module playground_solver_functions
   use forsolver, only: rk
   implicit none
contains
   function f(x) result(y)
      real(rk), intent(in) :: x
      real(rk) :: y
      y = x**3+x-2.0_rk
   end function
   function df(x) result(y)
      real(rk), intent(in) :: x
      real(rk) :: y
      y = 3.0_rk*x**2+1.0_rk
   end function
   function fc(x) result(y)
      complex(rk), intent(in) :: x
      complex(rk) :: y
      y = x**3+x-2.0_rk
   end function
end module

program demo_forsolver
   use forsolver, only: rk,nlsolver
   use playground_solver_functions, only: f,df,fc
   use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   implicit none
   type(nlsolver) :: solver
   real(rk) :: roots(3),residuals(3)
   complex(rk) :: z
   integer :: i
   call solver%set_options(nl_method='newton',maxit=100,TolFun=1e-12_rk,verbosity=0)
   call solver%solve(F=f,dFdx=df,x0=2.0_rk,x_sol=roots(1))
   call solver%set_options(nl_method='newton-quasi-fd',fdm_method='central', &
      fdm_tol=1e-6_rk,maxit=100,TolFun=1e-12_rk,verbosity=0)
   call solver%solve(F=f,x0=2.0_rk,x_sol=roots(2))
   call solver%set_options(nl_method='newton-quasi-cs',cs_tol=1e-20_rk, &
      maxit=100,TolFun=1e-12_rk,verbosity=0)
   call solver%solve(F=fc,x0=cmplx(2.0_rk,0.0_rk,rk),x_sol=z)
   roots(3) = real(z,rk)
   residuals = [(abs(f(roots(i))),i=1,3)]
   if (.not. all(ieee_is_finite(roots))) error stop 'Nonfinite root'
   if (abs(aimag(z))>1e-10_rk) error stop 'Unexpected complex root'
   if (any(abs(roots-1.0_rk)>1e-10_rk)) error stop 'Roots differ from exact solution'
   if (any(residuals>1e-10_rk)) error stop 'Residual too large'
   print '(a)', 'Solve x**3+x-2 = 0; the unique real root is 1.'
   print '(a,2es18.9)', 'Analytic derivative: ',roots(1),residuals(1)
   print '(a,2es18.9)', 'Central differences: ',roots(2),residuals(2)
   print '(a,2es18.9)', 'Complex step:        ',roots(3),residuals(3)
   print '(a)', 'PASS forsolver'
end program

description: Direct sparse LU factorization with pivoting, reordering and reuse for multiple right-hand sides.
source:
! Factor one sparse tridiagonal matrix, then solve two right-hand sides.
program demo_y12m
   use y12m, only: y12mb,y12mc,y12md
   use iso_fortran_env, only: wp => real64
   use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   implicit none
   integer, parameter :: n=8,nn=500
   real(wp) :: a(nn),pivot(n),b(n),original_rhs(n),flags(8),matrix(n,n),exact(n),residual
   integer :: columns(nn),rows(nn),ha(n,11),iflag(10),status,nz,i,j,load
   matrix = 0; a = 0; rows = 0; columns = 0; ha = 0; nz = 0
   do i=1,n
      matrix(i,i) = 3
      if (i<n) then
         matrix(i,i+1) = -1
         matrix(i+1,i) = -1
      end if
   end do
   do i=1,n
      do j=1,n
         if (matrix(i,j)==0) cycle
         nz = nz+1; a(nz) = matrix(i,j); rows(nz) = i; columns(nz) = j
      end do
   end do
   iflag = 0; flags = 0
   iflag(2:5) = [3,1,0,2] ! Keep L for subsequent right-hand sides.
   flags(1:4) = [16.0_wp,1e-12_wp,1e16_wp,1e-12_wp]
   exact = 1; b = matmul(matrix,exact)
   call y12mb(n,nz,a,columns,nn,rows,nn,ha,n,flags,iflag,status)
   if (status/=0) error stop 'Sparse preparation failed'
   call y12mc(n,nz,a,columns,nn,rows,nn,pivot,b,ha,n,flags,iflag,status)
   if (status/=0) error stop 'Sparse factorization failed'
   do load=1,2
      if (load==2) then
         exact = [(real(i,wp),i=1,n)]
         b = matmul(matrix,exact)
         iflag(5) = 3 ! Full forward/back substitution using stored factors.
      end if
      original_rhs = matmul(matrix,exact)
      call y12md(n,a,nn,b,pivot,columns,ha,n,iflag,status)
      if (status/=0) error stop 'Sparse solve failed'
      if (.not. all(ieee_is_finite(b))) error stop 'Nonfinite solution'
      residual = maxval(abs(matmul(matrix,b)-original_rhs))
      if (residual>1e-10_wp .or. maxval(abs(b-exact))>1e-10_wp) error stop 'Sparse solution differs'
      print '(a,i0,a,8f8.3)', 'Right-hand side ',load,', solution: ',b
      print '(a,es12.3)', 'Maximum residual: ',residual
   end do
   print '(a)', 'One LU factorization used for both right-hand sides.'
   print '(a)', 'PASS y12m'
end program

! Three unit masses and four unit springs, with both ends fixed.
program demo_foreig
   use kinds, only: rk
   use foreig, only: eig
   use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   implicit none
   real(rk) :: stiffness(3,3),workspace(3,3),identity(3,3),expected(3),residual,orthogonality
   real(rk), allocatable :: vectors(:,:),values(:)
   integer :: i
   stiffness = reshape([2.0_rk,-1.0_rk,0.0_rk,-1.0_rk,2.0_rk,-1.0_rk,0.0_rk,-1.0_rk,2.0_rk],[3,3])
   workspace = stiffness
   call eig(workspace,vectors,values,method='syev')
   if (.not. all(ieee_is_finite(values))) error stop 'Nonfinite eigenvalues'
   if (.not. all(ieee_is_finite(vectors))) error stop 'Nonfinite eigenvectors'
   identity = 0
   do i=1,3
      identity(i,i) = 1
      expected(i) = 2.0_rk-2.0_rk*cos(real(i,rk)*acos(-1.0_rk)/4.0_rk)
      residual = norm2(matmul(stiffness,vectors(:,i))-values(i)*vectors(:,i))
      if (residual>1e-11_rk) error stop 'Eigenpair residual too large'
   end do
   orthogonality = maxval(abs(matmul(transpose(vectors),vectors)-identity))
   if (orthogonality>1e-11_rk) error stop 'Eigenvectors are not orthonormal'
   if (maxval(abs(values-expected))>1e-11_rk) error stop 'Analytic eigenvalues differ'
   print '(a)', 'Mode    Squared angular frequency    Angular frequency'
   do i=1,3
      print '(i3,2f25.12)',i,values(i),sqrt(values(i))
   end do
   print '(a,es12.3)', 'Orthogonality error: ',orthogonality
   print '(a)', 'PASS foreig'
end program

   implicit none
   real(rk) :: y(2),t,target,relative,absolute,work(15),error,exact(2)

module playground_dogleg_fit
   use iso_c_binding, only: wp => c_double
   implicit none
contains
   subroutine residual(x,f,jac,params)
      real(wp), intent(in) :: x(:)
      real(wp), intent(out) :: f(:),jac(:,:)
      class(*), intent(in), optional :: params
      real(wp) :: time,exponential,observed
      integer :: i
      do i=1,size(f)
         time = real(i-1,wp)/5
         exponential = exp(-x(2)*time)
         observed = 2.5_wp*exp(-0.7_wp*time)

program demo_nafpack
   use NAFPack_kinds, only: sp
   use NAFPack_Fourier_Transform, only: Fourier_Transform,ALG_RADIX2_DIT,idft
   use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   implicit none
   integer, parameter :: n=16
   type(Fourier_Transform) :: transform
   complex(sp) :: signal(n),expected(n),spectrum(n)
   complex(sp), allocatable :: recovered(:)
   real(sp) :: theta,real_part(n),imaginary_part(n),spectrum_error,roundtrip_error
   integer :: i
   do i=1,n
      theta = 2*acos(-1.0_sp)*real(i-1,sp)/n
      signal(i) = cmplx(cos(3*theta),sin(3*theta),sp)+0.25_sp*cmplx(cos(5*theta),sin(5*theta),sp)
   end do
   expected = cmplx(0.0_sp,0.0_sp,sp)
   expected(4) = real(n,sp); expected(6) = real(n,sp)/4
   call transform%create_fft_plan_sp(n,algorithm=ALG_RADIX2_DIT)
   call transform%execute_fft_plan_sp(real(signal,sp),aimag(signal),real_part,imaginary_part)
   spectrum = cmplx(real_part,imaginary_part,sp)
   call transform%destroy_fft_plan_sp()
   recovered = idft(spectrum)
   if (.not. all(ieee_is_finite(real(spectrum)))) error stop 'Nonfinite spectrum'
   if (.not. all(ieee_is_finite(aimag(spectrum)))) error stop 'Nonfinite spectrum'
   if (.not. all(ieee_is_finite(real(recovered)))) error stop 'Nonfinite reconstruction'
   if (.not. all(ieee_is_finite(aimag(recovered)))) error stop 'Nonfinite reconstruction'
   spectrum_error = maxval(abs(spectrum-expected))
   roundtrip_error = maxval(abs(recovered-signal))
   if (spectrum_error>1e-4_sp) error stop 'Known frequency amplitudes differ'
   if (roundtrip_error>1e-5_sp) error stop 'Inverse transform differs'
   print '(a)', 'Sixteen complex samples: frequency 3 plus frequency 5 at quarter amplitude.'
   print '(a)', 'Frequency   Fourier amplitude'
   do i=1,n
      if (abs(spectrum(i))>1e-4_sp) print '(i6,f20.8)',i-1,abs(spectrum(i))
   end do
   print '(a,es12.3)', 'Maximum spectral error: ',spectrum_error
   print '(a,es12.3)', 'Maximum round-trip error: ',roundtrip_error
   print '(a)', 'PASS nafpack'
end program

program demo_fishpack
   use fishpack, only: wp, ip, hwscrt
   use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   implicit none
   integer(ip), parameter :: n=32
   real(wp) :: f(n+1,n+1), exact(n+1,n+1), boundary(n+1), pi, x, y, perturbation, err
   integer(ip) :: i,j,status
   pi = acos(-1._wp)
   boundary = 0
   f = 0
   do j=1,n+1
      y = real(j-1,wp)/n
      do i=1,n+1
         x = real(i-1,wp)/n
         exact(i,j) = sin(pi*x)*sin(pi*y)
         if (i>1 .and. i<n+1 .and. j>1 .and. j<n+1) f(i,j) = -2*pi*pi*exact(i,j)
      end do
   end do
   call hwscrt(0._wp,1._wp,n,1_ip,boundary,boundary,0._wp,1._wp,n,1_ip, &
      boundary,boundary,0._wp,f,n+1,perturbation,status)
   if (status/=0) error stop 'Poisson solver failed'
   if (.not. all(ieee_is_finite(f))) error stop 'Nonfinite solution'
   err = maxval(abs(f-exact))
   print '(a,i0,a,i0)', 'Grid intervals: ',n,' x ',n
   print '(a,f16.10)', 'Computed center value: ',f(n/2+1,n/2+1)
   print '(a,es12.3)', 'Maximum discretization error: ',err
   if (err>1e-3_wp) error stop 'Poisson error exceeds second-order tolerance'
   print '(a)', 'PASS fishpack'
end program

! Adapted from the author's delay_oscillator test: y'(t)=-y(t-pi/2), history sin(t).
! The exact solution remains sin(t). Keep callbacks in a module.
module playground_delay_callbacks
   implicit none
contains
   subroutine rhs(t,y,z,dy)
      double precision, intent(in) :: t,y(:),z(:,:)
      double precision, intent(out) :: dy(:)
      dy(1) = -z(1,1)
   end subroutine
   subroutine history(t,y)
      double precision, intent(in) :: t
      double precision, intent(out) :: y(:)
      y(1) = sin(t)
   end subroutine
end module
program demo_dde_solver
   use playground_delay_callbacks
   use dde_solver_m, only: dde_set, dde_solver, dde_sol, dde_opts, dde_int, &
      dde_val, release_arrays, release_int
   use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   implicit none
   type(dde_sol) :: sol
   type(dde_opts) :: opts
   type(dde_int) :: sampled
   double precision :: pi, times(9), err
   integer :: i
   pi = acos(-1d0)
   opts = dde_set(re=1d-9,ae=1d-12,interpolation=.true.)
   sol = dde_solver([1,1],rhs,[pi/2],history,[0d0,2*pi],options=opts)
   if (sol%flag/=0) error stop 'Delay solver failed'
   times = [(real(i,kind(pi))*pi/4,i=0,8)]
   sampled = dde_val(times,sol)
   if (.not. all(ieee_is_finite(sampled%yt))) error stop 'Nonfinite delay solution'
   err = maxval(abs(sampled%yt(:,1)-sin(times)))
   print '(a)', 'Time             Numerical y          Exact y'
   do i=1,size(times)
      print '(3f20.10)', times(i),sampled%yt(i,1),sin(times(i))
   end do
   print '(a,es12.3)', 'Maximum error: ',err
   if (err>1d-7) error stop 'Delay solution inaccurate'
   call release_arrays(sol,opts)
   call release_int(sampled)
   print '(a)', 'PASS dde_solver'
end program

! Spherical Helmholtz example adapted from the author's examples/helmsph.f90.
! Exact solution (1+x*y)*exp(z) on the unit sphere, lambda=1.
program demo_spherepack
   use spherepack, only: GaussianSphere, wp, ip
   use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   implicit none
   integer(ip), parameter :: nlat=19,nlon=36
   type(GaussianSphere) :: globe
   real(wp) :: exact(nlat,nlon), rhs(nlat,nlon), solution(nlat,nlon), x,y,z,err
   integer :: i,j
   globe = GaussianSphere(nlat,nlon)
   do j=1,nlon
      do i=1,nlat
         x = globe%unit_vectors%radial(i,j)%x
         y = globe%unit_vectors%radial(i,j)%y
         z = globe%unit_vectors%radial(i,j)%z
         exact(i,j) = (1+x*y)*exp(z)
         rhs(i,j) = -(x*y*(z*z+6*(z+1))+z*(z+2))*exp(z)
      end do
   end do
   call globe%invert_helmholtz(1._wp,rhs,solution)
   if (.not. all(ieee_is_finite(solution))) error stop 'Nonfinite spherical solution'
   err = maxval(abs(solution-exact))
   print '(a,i0,a,i0)', 'Gaussian spherical grid: ',nlat,' x ',nlon
   print '(a,es12.3)', 'Maximum Helmholtz solution error: ',err
   if (err>1e-10_wp) error stop 'Spherical Helmholtz solve inaccurate'
   call globe%destroy()
   print '(a)', 'PASS spherepack'
end program

description: Singular value decomposition and truncated low-rank matrix approximations.
source:
! Compare rank-one and rank-two approximations of a small matrix.
program demo_forsvd
   use kinds, only: rk
   use forsvd, only: svd
   use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   implicit none
   real(rk) :: a(4,3), work(4,3), u(4,4), s(3), vt(3,3), approx(4,3), errors(3)
   integer :: i,j,k
   a = reshape([3._rk,0._rk,0._rk,0._rk,0._rk,2._rk,0._rk,0._rk,0._rk,0._rk,1._rk,0._rk],[4,3])
   ! LAPACK overwrites its input workspace; preserve A for independent checks.
   work = a
   call svd(work,u,s,vt,method='gesvd')
   if (.not. all(ieee_is_finite(s))) error stop 'Nonfinite singular values'
   if (.not. all(ieee_is_finite(u)) .or. .not. all(ieee_is_finite(vt))) error stop 'Nonfinite vectors'
   if (maxval(abs(s-[3._rk,2._rk,1._rk]))>1e-11_rk) error stop 'Incorrect singular values'
   approx = 0
   print '(a)', 'Rank    Frobenius reconstruction error'
   do k=1,3
      do j=1,3
         do i=1,4
            approx(i,j) = approx(i,j)+s(k)*u(i,k)*vt(k,j)
         end do
      end do
      errors(k) = norm2(a-approx)
      print '(i3,es22.10)', k, errors(k)
   end do
   if (maxval(abs(errors-[sqrt(5._rk),1._rk,0._rk]))>1e-11_rk) error stop 'Incorrect approximation'
   print '(a)', 'PASS forsvd'
end program

gams_procedures.notes: Computes real dense SVD using LAPACK GESVD or GESDD; the demonstration preserves a separate input copy.

! Gauss-Legendre and Gauss-Hermite rules with independently known integrals.
program demo_qdutillib
   use QDUtil_NumParameters_m, only: Rkind
   use QDUtil_Quadrature_m, only: Quadrature_t, Init_Quadrature, dealloc_Quadrature
   use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   implicit none
   type(Quadrature_t) :: q
   real(Rkind) :: value, exact
   integer :: status
   call Init_Quadrature(q,nq=6,name='LegendreP',err=status)
   if (status/=0) error stop 'Legendre initialization failed'
   value = sum(q%w*q%x(1,:)**8)
   exact = 2._Rkind/9._Rkind
   print '(a,f20.14,a,es12.3)', 'Integral of x**8 on [-1,1]: ',value,'  error: ',abs(value-exact)
   if (.not. ieee_is_finite(value)) error stop 'Nonfinite integral'
   if (abs(value-exact)>1e-12_Rkind) error stop 'Legendre quadrature failed'
   call dealloc_Quadrature(q)
   call Init_Quadrature(q,nq=8,name='HO',err=status)
   if (status/=0) error stop 'Hermite initialization failed'
   ! HO weights integrate the full function: include the Gaussian explicitly.
   value = sum(q%w*q%x(1,:)**2*exp(-q%x(1,:)**2))
   exact = sqrt(acos(-1._Rkind))/2._Rkind
   print '(a,f20.14,a,es12.3)', 'Integral of x**2*exp(-x**2): ',value,'  error: ',abs(value-exact)
   if (.not. ieee_is_finite(value)) error stop 'Nonfinite integral'
   if (abs(value-exact)>1e-12_Rkind) error stop 'Hermite quadrature failed'
   call dealloc_Quadrature(q)
   print '(a)', 'PASS qdutillib'
end program

description: Sparse LDL-transpose factorization, orderings and solves for quasi-definite systems.
source:
! Solve a small quasi-definite KKT system using three sparse orderings.
program demo_qdldl
   use qdldl_module, only: qdldl_type, wp=>qdldl_wp, ip=>qdldl_ip, qdldl_success, &
      qdldl_order_natural, qdldl_order_rcm, qdldl_order_amd
   use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   implicit none
   integer(ip), parameter :: n=4
   integer(ip), parameter :: row(*)=[1,2,1,2,3,1,2,4], col(*)=[1,2,3,3,3,4,4,4]
   real(wp), parameter :: val(*)=[4._wp,3._wp,1._wp,2._wp,-2._wp,-1._wp,1._wp,-1._wp]
   integer, parameter :: order(*)=[qdldl_order_natural,qdldl_order_rcm,qdldl_order_amd]
   character(7), parameter :: names(*)=['natural','RCM    ','AMD    ']
   type(qdldl_type) :: solver
   real(wp) :: a(n,n), rhs(n), x(n), exact(n), err, residual
   integer :: i,k,status
   integer(ip) :: positive,negative,zero
   a=0
   do k=1,size(val)
      a(row(k),col(k))=val(k)
      a(col(k),row(k))=val(k)
   end do
   exact=[1._wp,-2._wp,3._wp,-4._wp]
   rhs=matmul(a,exact)
   print '(a)', 'Ordering   Max solution error   Max residual   Inertia (+,-,0)'
   do i=1,size(order)
      block
         type(qdldl_type) :: factor
         call factor%analyze(n,row,col,status,ordering=order(i))
         if (status/=qdldl_success) error stop 'Sparse analysis failed'
         call factor%factor(val,status)
         if (status/=qdldl_success) error stop 'Sparse factorization failed'
         x=rhs
         call factor%solve(x,status)
         if (status/=qdldl_success) error stop 'Sparse solve failed'
         if (.not.all(ieee_is_finite(x))) error stop 'Nonfinite solution'
         call factor%inertia(positive,negative,zero)
         err=maxval(abs(x-exact))
         residual=maxval(abs(matmul(a,x)-rhs))
         print '(a7,2es19.3,3i4)', names(i),err,residual,positive,negative,zero
         if (max(err,residual)>1e-11_wp) error stop 'Sparse solution inaccurate'
         if (positive/=2 .or. negative/=2 .or. zero/=0) error stop 'Incorrect matrix inertia'
      end block
   end do
   print '(a)', 'PASS qdldl-fortran'
end program

description: Sparse LU factorization, linear solves and efficient column updates.
source:
! Factor a sparse matrix once, replace one column, and update the LU factors.
program demo_lusol
   use lusol, only: lu1fac,lu6sol,lu8rpc
   use lusol_precision, only: ip,wp=>rp
   use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   implicit none
   integer(ip), parameter :: n=4, capacity=10000
   integer(ip) :: indc(capacity),indr(capacity),p(n),q(n),lenc(n),lenr(n),locc(n),locr(n)
   integer(ip) :: iploc(n),iqloc(n),ipinv(n),iqinv(n),luparm(30),status,i,j,k
   real(wp) :: a(capacity),parmlu(30),work(n),v(n),x(n),dense(n,n),exact(n),rhs(n),diag,vnorm
   a=0; indc=0; indr=0
   dense=0
   do i=1,n
      dense(i,i)=4
      if (i<n) then
         dense(i,i+1)=-1
         dense(i+1,i)=-1
      end if
   end do
   k=0
   do j=1,n
      do i=1,n
         if (dense(i,j)==0) cycle
         k=k+1; indc(k)=i; indr(k)=j; a(k)=dense(i,j)
      end do
   end do
   ! Parameter initialization follows the upstream lusol_ez wrapper.
   luparm=0
   luparm(1)=6; luparm(3)=5; luparm(8)=1
   parmlu=0
   parmlu(1:8)=[100._wp,10._wp,epsilon(1._wp)**0.8_wp, &
      epsilon(1._wp)**0.67_wp,epsilon(1._wp)**0.67_wp,3._wp,0.3_wp,0.5_wp]
   call lu1fac(n,n,k,capacity,luparm,parmlu,a,indc,indr,p,q,lenc,lenr,locc,locr, &
      iploc,iqloc,ipinv,iqinv,work,status)
   if (status/=0) error stop 'LU factorization failed'
   exact=[1._wp,-2._wp,3._wp,-4._wp]
   call check_solution('Original system')
   dense(:,2)=[0.5_wp,5._wp,-0.5_wp,0.25_wp]
   v=dense(:,2)
   call lu8rpc(1_ip,1_ip,n,n,2_ip,v,work,capacity,luparm,parmlu,a,indc,indr,p,q, &
      lenc,lenr,locc,locr,status,diag,vnorm)
   if (status/=0) error stop 'Column update failed'
   call check_solution('After replacing column 2')
   print '(a)', 'PASS lusol'
contains
   subroutine check_solution(label)
      character(*),intent(in) :: label
      real(wp) :: err,residual
      rhs=matmul(dense,exact)
      v=rhs
      call lu6sol(5_ip,n,n,v,x,capacity,luparm,parmlu,a,indc,indr,p,q,lenc,lenr,locc,locr,status)
      if (status/=0) error stop 'LU solve failed'
      if (.not.all(ieee_is_finite(x))) error stop 'Nonfinite solution'
      err=maxval(abs(x-exact)); residual=maxval(abs(matmul(dense,x)-rhs))
      print '(a)', label
      print '(a,4f12.7)', 'Solution: ',x
      print '(a,2es14.3)', 'Solution error and residual: ',err,residual
      if (max(err,residual)>1e-11_wp) error stop 'LU solution inaccurate'
   end subroutine
end program

description: Carlson symmetric elliptic integrals for pendulum periods and other applications.
source:
! Pendulum period beyond the small-angle approximation, using Carlson RF.
program demo_carlson
   use carlson_elliptic_module, only: wp=>carlson_elliptic_module_wp,drf
   use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   implicit none
   integer,parameter :: intervals=4096
   real(wp),parameter :: angles(*)=[0._wp,30._wp,90._wp,150._wp],gravity=9.80665_wp
   real(wp) :: pi,k,elliptic,reference,h,t,sum_integral,period,error
   integer :: i,j,status
   pi=acos(-1._wp)
   if (abs(drf(1._wp,1._wp,1._wp)-1._wp)>1e-13_wp) error stop 'RF identity failed'
   print '(a)', 'Amplitude (deg)  Period for L=1 m (s)   Ratio to small-angle   Quadrature error'
   do i=1,size(angles)
      k=sin(angles(i)*pi/360)
      elliptic=drf(0._wp,1-k*k,1._wp,status)
      if (status/=0) error stop 'Elliptic integral failed'
      ! Independent composite Simpson integration of the defining integral.
      h=pi/(2*intervals)
      sum_integral=1._wp+1/sqrt(1-k*k)
      do j=1,intervals-1
         t=j*h
         sum_integral=sum_integral+merge(4._wp,2._wp,mod(j,2)==1)/sqrt(1-(k*sin(t))**2)
      end do
      reference=h*sum_integral/3
      error=abs(elliptic-reference)
      if (.not.ieee_is_finite(elliptic)) error stop 'Nonfinite integral'
      if (error>1e-10_wp) error stop 'Elliptic integral differs from quadrature'
      period=4*elliptic/sqrt(gravity)
      print '(f12.1,2f23.12,es20.3)',angles(i),period,2*elliptic/pi,error
   end do
   print '(a)', 'PASS carlson-elliptic-integrals'
end program

gams_procedures.notes: Carlson symmetric RF evaluated for pendulum periods and checked against independent composite Simpson integration.

! Frequency response of m*x''+c*x'+k*x=cos(omega*t).
module playground_dynamics_force
   use, intrinsic :: iso_fortran_env, only: real64
   implicit none
contains
   subroutine unit_force(frequency,force,args)
      real(real64),intent(in) :: frequency
      complex(real64),intent(out) :: force(:)
      class(*),optional,intent(inout) :: args
      force=cmplx(1._real64,0._real64,real64)
   end subroutine
end module
program demo_dynamics
   use playground_dynamics_force
   use dynamics, only: frf,frequency_response,modal_excite
   use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   implicit none
   real(real64),parameter :: omega(*)=[0._real64,0.5_real64,1._real64,1.5_real64, &
      2._real64,2.5_real64,3._real64,4._real64]
   real(real64) :: mass(1,1),stiffness(1,1),err
   complex(real64) :: exact
   type(frf) :: response
   procedure(modal_excite),pointer :: forcing
   integer :: i
   mass=1; stiffness=4
   forcing=>unit_force
   ! C=alpha*M+beta*K, so alpha=0.2 and beta=0 give damping c=0.2.
   response=frequency_response(mass,stiffness,0.2_real64,0._real64,omega,forcing)
   if (.not.allocated(response%responses)) error stop 'No frequency response'
   if (size(response%responses,1)/=size(omega)) error stop 'Wrong frequency count'
   if (.not.all(ieee_is_finite(abs(response%responses)))) error stop 'Nonfinite response'
   print '(a)', 'Angular frequency    Displacement amplitude    Analytic error'
   do i=1,size(omega)
      exact=1/cmplx(4-omega(i)**2,0.2_real64*omega(i),real64)
      err=abs(response%responses(i,1)-exact)
      print '(f14.5,f26.12,es18.3)',omega(i),abs(response%responses(i,1)),err
      if (err>1e-10_real64) error stop 'Frequency response differs from analytic solution'
   end do
   print '(a)', 'PASS dynamics'
end program

description: Forward and reverse automatic differentiation with array computation graphs.
source:
! Array and forward-mode setup follows test/test_functions.f90 (MIT).
! f(x1,x2) = x1*x2**2 + x1**2; compare analytical and AD gradients.
program main
   use diffstruc
   use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   implicit none
   type(array_type) :: x
   type(array_type), pointer :: f, derivative
   real(real32) :: forward(2), reverse(2), exact(2), direction(2), err
   integer :: j

   call x%allocate(array_shape=[2,1])
   x%is_temporary = .false.
   x%val(:,1) = [1.25_real32, -2._real32]
   call x%set_requires_grad(.true.)
   f => pack(x,[1],1)*pack(x,[2],1)**2 + pack(x,[1],1)**2
   f%is_temporary = .false.
   exact = [x%val(2,1)**2+2*x%val(1,1), 2*x%val(1,1)*x%val(2,1)]
   do j = 1, 2
      direction = 0._real32
      direction(j) = 1._real32
      call x%set_direction(direction)
      derivative => f%grad_forward(x)
      derivative%is_temporary = .false.
      forward(j) = derivative%val(1,1)
   end do
   ! Reverse accumulation also uses direction: enable both components.
   call x%set_direction([1._real32,1._real32])
   call f%grad_reverse(reset_graph=.true.)
   if (.not. associated(x%grad)) error stop 'No reverse gradient'
   reverse = x%grad%val(:,1)
   err = max(maxval(abs(forward-exact)),maxval(abs(reverse-exact)))
   print '(a,f12.6)', 'Function value = ', f%val(1,1)
   print '(a,2f12.6)', 'Analytical gradient: ', exact
   print '(a,2f12.6)', 'Forward gradient:    ', forward
   print '(a,2f12.6)', 'Reverse gradient:    ', reverse
   if (.not. ieee_is_finite(err) .or. err > 1.e-5_real32) error stop 'Incorrect gradient'
   print *, 'PASS diffstruc'
end program main

gams_procedures.notes: Forward directional derivatives and reverse-mode gradients of array expressions; the demo restores the direction mask before reverse accumulation.

description: Complex dual numbers for derivatives through configurable order.
source:
! Dual-number setup follows the author's app/ex1.f90 (MIT).
program main
   use config_mod, only: prec
   use dualzn_mod
   use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   implicit none
   type(dualzn) :: x, y
   complex(prec) :: z, exact
   real(prec) :: err
   integer :: k, sample

   print *, 'Derivatives 0 through 5 of exp(z) + sin(z)'
   do sample = 1, 2
      z = cmplx(0.4_prec, 0.2_prec*(sample-1), kind=prec)
      x = xto_dzn(0, 5)
      x%f(0) = z
      x%f(1) = 1.0_prec
      y = exp(x) + sin(x)
      print '(a,2f9.4)', 'z (real, imaginary) = ', real(z), aimag(z)
      do k = 0, 5
         select case (mod(k,4))
         case (0)
            exact = exp(z) + sin(z)
         case (1)
            exact = exp(z) + cos(z)
         case (2)
            exact = exp(z) - sin(z)
         case (3)
            exact = exp(z) - cos(z)
         end select
         err = abs(y%f(k)-exact)
         if (.not. ieee_is_finite(err) .or. err > 2.e-12_prec) error stop 'Incorrect derivative'
         print '(i2,2f15.10,a,es10.2)', k, real(y%f(k)), aimag(y%f(k)), ' error ', err
      end do
   end do
   print *, 'PASS dnaoad-fpm'
end program main

gams_procedures.notes: Dual-number derivatives through the configured maximum order (five in this build); the demo checks orders zero through five at real and complex arguments.

program main

   implicit none
   type(optim_type) :: optim
   real :: x(2), grad(2), cost, exact_cost, exact_grad(2)
   integer :: flag, calls

   x = [1.5, 1.5]
   call Rosenbrock(x, cost, grad)
   call set_inputs(optim, cost, 1000, conv=1.e-12, l=10, print_flag=0)
   flag = 0
   calls = 0

      calls = calls + 1

      call LBFGS(2, x, cost, grad, optim, flag)
      if (flag == 1) call Rosenbrock(x, cost, grad)
   end do
   exact_cost = (1.-x(1))**2 + 100.*(x(2)-x(1)**2)**2
   exact_grad = [2.*(x(1)-1.)-400.*x(1)*(x(2)-x(1)**2), 200.*(x(2)-x(1)**2)]
   if (flag /= 2 .or. .not. all(ieee_is_finite(x))) error stop 'Optimizer failed'

   if (maxval(abs(exact_grad)) > 2.e-3) error stop 'Gradient too large'
   print '(a,2f13.8)', 'Rosenbrock minimum x = ', x
   print '(a,es12.4)', 'Objective = ', exact_cost
   print '(a,i0)', 'Iterations = ', optim%cpt_iter

description: Geostatistical covariance models, kriging and spatial simulation routines.
source:
! Ordinary kriging from two observations using GSLIB covariance and solver routines.
! No data files: observations are value 1 at x=0 and value 3 at x=2.
program main
   use, intrinsic :: iso_fortran_env, only: real64
   use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   implicit none
   real(real64) :: rotation(1,3,3), a(6), rhs(3), weights(3), original_rhs(3)
   real(real64) :: matrix(3,3), corr, expected(3), residual, variance, estimate
   real :: c0(1), cc(1), ranges(1), cmax, covariance, point
   integer :: nst(1), model(1), i, j, k, status, sample
   interface
      subroutine cova3(x1,y1,z1,x2,y2,z2,ivarg,nst,maxnst,c0,it,cc,aa,irot,maxrot,rotmat,cmax,cova)
         import real64
         real :: x1,y1,z1,x2,y2,z2,c0(*),cc(*),aa(*),cmax,cova
         integer :: ivarg,nst(*),maxnst,it(*),irot,maxrot
         real(real64) :: rotmat(maxrot,3,3)
      end subroutine
      subroutine ksol(nright,neq,nsb,a,r,s,ising)
         import real64
         integer :: nright,neq,nsb,ising
         real(real64) :: a(*),r(*),s(*)
      end subroutine
   end interface

   ! Identity rotation; unit sill, zero nugget, exponential covariance exp(-h).
   rotation = 0._real64
   do i = 1, 3
      rotation(1,i,i) = 1._real64
   end do
   nst = 1
   model = 2
   c0 = 0.
   cc = 1.
   ranges = 3.
   call cova3(0.,0.,0.,2.,0.,0.,1,nst,1,c0,model,cc,ranges,1,1,rotation,cmax,covariance)
   corr = real(covariance,real64)
   if (abs(corr-exp(-2._real64)) > 2.e-7_real64) error stop 'Wrong covariance'
   matrix = reshape([1._real64,corr,1._real64,corr,1._real64,1._real64, &
                     1._real64,1._real64,0._real64],[3,3])
   print *, 'Position    Kriging estimate    Variance    System residual'
   do sample = 0, 4
      point = 0.5*sample
      do i = 1, 2
         call cova3(real(2*(i-1)),0.,0.,point,0.,0.,1,nst,1,c0,model,cc,ranges, &
                    1,1,rotation,cmax,covariance)
         rhs(i) = real(covariance,real64)
         if (abs(rhs(i)-exp(-abs(real(point,real64)-2*(i-1)))) > 2.e-7_real64) &
            error stop 'Wrong target covariance'
      end do
      rhs(3) = 1._real64
      original_rhs = rhs
      k = 0
      do j = 1, 3
         do i = 1, j
            k = k+1
            a(k) = matrix(i,j)
         end do
      end do
      call ksol(1,3,1,a,rhs,weights,status)
      if (status /= 0 .or. .not. all(ieee_is_finite(weights))) error stop 'Kriging solve failed'
      expected(1) = 0.5_real64*(1._real64+(original_rhs(1)-original_rhs(2))/(1._real64-corr))
      expected(2) = 1._real64-expected(1)
      expected(3) = original_rhs(1)-expected(1)-corr*expected(2)
      residual = maxval(abs(matmul(matrix,weights)-original_rhs))
      if (maxval(abs(weights-expected)) > 1.e-10_real64 .or. residual > 1.e-10_real64) &
         error stop 'Wrong kriging weights'
      estimate = weights(1)+3._real64*weights(2)
      variance = 1._real64-dot_product(weights(1:2),original_rhs(1:2))-weights(3)
      if (.not. ieee_is_finite(estimate) .or. variance < -1.e-10_real64) error stop 'Invalid estimate'
      if (sample == 0 .and. abs(estimate-1._real64) > 1.e-10_real64) error stop 'Endpoint mismatch'
      if (sample == 2 .and. abs(estimate-2._real64) > 1.e-10_real64) error stop 'Midpoint mismatch'
      if (sample == 4 .and. abs(estimate-3._real64) > 1.e-10_real64) error stop 'Endpoint mismatch'
      print '(f8.2,2f18.8,es18.3)', point, estimate, variance, residual
   end do
   print *, 'PASS gslib'
end program main

gams_procedures.notes: The driver assembles an ordinary-kriging system from GSLIB covariance and linear-solver routines. It checks exponential covariances, closed-form weights, endpoint interpolation and independent system residuals. Broad interpolation/covariance classes only; no exhaustive spatial-statistics review.

description: Radial Schroedinger and Dirac equations solved with high-order finite elements.
source:
! Setup adapted from the author's test/test_coulomb_schroed.f90 (MIT).
! A one-electron hydrogen Coulomb potential, in atomic units (Hartree energies).
program main
   use types, only: dp
   use schroed_dirac_solver, only: total_energy
   use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   implicit none
   integer, parameter :: ne = 8, p = 20, nq = 43
   real(dp) :: alpha_j(-7:6), alpha(-7:6), quadrature(nq,ne), error, exact
   real(dp), allocatable :: energies(:), wavefunctions(:,:,:)
   integer :: dofs, principal, angular, index

   alpha = 0._dp
   alpha_j = -2._dp
   call total_energy(1,100._dp,ne,100._dp,p,nq,dofs,0,0,137.0359895_dp,0, &
                     -7,alpha_j,alpha,energies,wavefunctions,quadrature)
   if (.not. all(ieee_is_finite(energies))) error stop 'Nonfinite energy'
   print '(a,i0)', 'Radial finite-element degrees of freedom: ', dofs
   print *, ' n  l        Energy (Hartree)          Exact            Absolute error'
   do principal = 1, 3
      exact = -0.5_dp/real(principal**2,dp)
      do angular = 0, principal-1
         index = (principal-1)*principal/2+angular+1
         error = abs(energies(index)-exact)
         print '(2i3,2f21.12,es15.3)', principal,angular,energies(index),exact,error
         if (error > 1.e-7_dp) error stop 'Hydrogen energy check failed'
      end do
   end do
   print *, 'PASS featom'
end program main

gams_procedures.notes: Radial one-dimensional boundary-value eigenproblem solved by finite elements. The demo checks the six n<=3 hydrogen Coulomb energies; no claim of validating the relativistic or self-consistent DFT paths.

description: Markov chains, stochastic-process discretization and numerical tools for economic models.
source:
! Calls follow the author's test/markov_test.f90 and test/tauchen_test.f90 (MIT).
! markov_steady_state expects COLUMN-stochastic transitions.
! tauchen returns ROW-stochastic transitions, so transpose before iteration.
program main
   use shared_mod, only: wp
   use dist_mod, only: markov_steady_state, tauchen
   use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   implicit none
   integer, parameter :: n = 31
   real(wp) :: transition(2,2), stationary(2), reference(2), residual
   real(wp) :: nodes(n), probabilities(n,n), distribution(n), mean, variance, exact_variance
   integer :: status

   transition(1,:) = [0.9_wp,0.2_wp]
   transition(2,:) = [0.1_wp,0.8_wp]
   stationary = 0._wp
   call markov_steady_state(transition,stationary,1.e-14_wp,10000,status)
   reference = [2._wp/3._wp,1._wp/3._wp]
   residual = maxval(abs(matmul(transition,stationary)-stationary))
   if (status /= 0 .or. .not. all(ieee_is_finite(stationary))) error stop 'Stationary iteration failed'
   if (maxval(abs(stationary-reference)) > 1.e-12_wp .or. residual > 1.e-12_wp) &
      error stop 'Wrong stationary distribution'
   print '(a,2f15.10)', 'Two-state equilibrium: ', stationary
   print '(a,es12.4)', 'Equilibrium residual: ', residual

   call tauchen(n,0._wp,0.8_wp,0.1_wp,3._wp,nodes,probabilities)
   if (.not. all(ieee_is_finite(probabilities))) error stop 'Nonfinite probability'
   if (minval(probabilities) < 0._wp .or. maxval(abs(sum(probabilities,dim=2)-1._wp)) > 1.e-12_wp) &
      error stop 'Invalid transition probabilities'
   distribution = 0._wp
   call markov_steady_state(transpose(probabilities),distribution,1.e-14_wp,10000,status)
   if (status /= 0 .or. .not. all(ieee_is_finite(distribution))) error stop 'Tauchen iteration failed'
   residual = maxval(abs(matmul(transpose(probabilities),distribution)-distribution))
   if (minval(distribution) < 0._wp .or. abs(sum(distribution)-1._wp) > 1.e-11_wp &
       .or. residual > 1.e-12_wp) error stop 'Invalid Tauchen stationary distribution'
   mean = dot_product(distribution,nodes)
   variance = dot_product(distribution,(nodes-mean)**2)
   exact_variance = 0.1_wp**2/(1._wp-0.8_wp**2)
   ! Finite-grid/truncated AR(1) approximation: variance need not be exact.
   if (abs(mean) > 1.e-11_wp .or. abs(variance-exact_variance) > 0.05_wp*exact_variance) &
      error stop 'Unexpected AR(1) approximation error'
   print '(a,i0)', 'Tauchen AR(1) states: ', n
   print '(a,es12.4)', 'Mean: ', mean
   print '(a,2f15.10)', 'Discrete and continuous variance: ', variance,exact_variance
   print '(a,es12.4)', 'Equilibrium residual: ', residual
   print *, 'PASS econ-toolchain'
end program main

gams_procedures.notes: Stochastic-process modeling: deterministic stationary probabilities and AR(1) Markov discretization, not a claim of random sampling. The stationary routine uses column-stochastic matrices, while tauchen returns row-stochastic matrices; the consumer transposes explicitly.

description: Magic squares, reduced row-echelon forms and other small matrix utilities.
source:
program demo_magic_squares
   use M_LA, only: mat_magic
   implicit none
   double precision, allocatable :: square(:, :)
   integer :: n, i, k, target, diagonal, reverse_diagonal

   print '(a)', 'Magic squares: order and common row/column/diagonal sum'
   do n = 3, 6
      allocate(square(n, n))
      call mat_magic(square, n, n)
      target = n*(n*n + 1)/2
      do i = 1, n
         if (nint(sum(square(i, :))) /= target) error stop 'row sum'
         if (nint(sum(square(:, i))) /= target) error stop 'column sum'
      end do
      diagonal = 0
      reverse_diagonal = 0
      do i = 1, n
         diagonal = diagonal + nint(square(i, i))
         reverse_diagonal = reverse_diagonal + nint(square(i, n + 1 - i))
      end do
      if (diagonal /= target .or. reverse_diagonal /= target) error stop 'diagonal sum'
      do k = 1, n*n
         if (count(nint(square) == k) /= 1) error stop 'entries must be a permutation of 1..n*n'
      end do
      print '(i3, i8)', n, target
      deallocate(square)
   end do
   print '(a)', 'PASS m_la'
end program demo_magic_squares

gams_procedures.notes: Matrix construction, illustrated by magic squares of orders three through six with independent row, column, diagonal and permutation checks. This mapping does not classify every other M_LA procedure.

description: Typed vectors and 4-by-4 matrices for geometric transformations.
source:
program demo_geometric_math
   use, intrinsic :: iso_c_binding, only: c_float, c_double
   use vector_3d, only: vec3d
   use matrix_4f, only: mat4f
   implicit none
   type(vec3d) :: a, b, c
   type(mat4f) :: transform
   real(c_float) :: point(4), result(4), matrix(4, 4)

   a = vec3d([1.0_c_double, 2.0_c_double, 3.0_c_double])
   b = vec3d([4.0_c_double, -1.0_c_double, 2.0_c_double])
   c = a + b
   if (any(abs(c%as_array() - [5.0_c_double, 1.0_c_double, 5.0_c_double]) > 1.e-12_c_double)) &
      error stop 'vector addition'
   c = a*b
   if (any(abs(c%as_array() - [4.0_c_double, -2.0_c_double, 6.0_c_double]) > 1.e-12_c_double)) &
      error stop 'component multiplication'
   print '(a, f8.3)', 'Dot product from component multiplication: ', sum(c%as_array())

   point = [1.0_c_float, 2.0_c_float, 3.0_c_float, 1.0_c_float]
   call transform%translate(10.0_c_float, -2.0_c_float, 1.0_c_float)
   matrix = reshape(transform%data, [4, 4])
   result = matmul(matrix, point)
   if (maxval(abs(result - [11.0_c_float, 0.0_c_float, 4.0_c_float, 1.0_c_float])) > 5.e-6_c_float) &
      error stop 'translation'
   print '(a, 3f9.3)', 'Translated point: ', result(:3)

   call transform%identity()
   call transform%rotate_z(acos(-1.0_c_float)/2)
   result = matmul(reshape(transform%data, [4, 4]), [1.0_c_float, 0.0_c_float, 0.0_c_float, 1.0_c_float])
   if (maxval(abs(result - [0.0_c_float, 1.0_c_float, 0.0_c_float, 1.0_c_float])) > 5.e-6_c_float) &
      error stop 'quarter-turn rotation'
   print '(a, 3f9.3)', 'Unit x vector rotated 90 degrees about z: ', result(:3)
   print '(a)', 'PASS fglm'
end program demo_geometric_math

gams_procedures.notes: Vector addition and component products, and column-major homogeneous translation and rotation matrices. The example checks a known point and a quarter-turn about z; broader geometry functionality is not exhaustively validated.

program demo_named_columns

description: Decimal-string arithmetic and signed or unsigned formatting of long integers.
source:
program demo_decimal_strings
   use, intrinsic :: iso_fortran_env, only: int64
   use strith, only: strint_type, new_strint, to_string, digits, int64_min, int64_max
   implicit none
   type(strint_type) :: a, b, total, recovered
   character(:), allocatable :: unsigned_value, decimal

   ! Interpret the all-one bit pattern as unsigned, without overflowing int64.
   unsigned_value = to_string(-1_int64, remove_0_padding=.true., as_unsigned=.true.)
   if (unsigned_value /= '18446744073709551615') error stop 'unsigned int64 formatting'
   print '(a)', 'Unsigned 64-bit maximum: '//unsigned_value

   ! The string constructor requires a sign and exactly digits-1 decimal digits.
   a = new_strint('+'//repeat('0', digits - 21)//'18446744073709551615')
   b = new_strint(1_int64)
   total = a + b
   decimal = total%to_string(remove_0_padding=.true.)
   if (decimal /= '18446744073709551616') error stop 'carry beyond 64 bits'
   print '(a)', 'Add one using decimal strings: '//decimal
   recovered = total - b
   if (recovered /= a) error stop 'subtraction round trip'
   a = new_strint(int64_min)
   b = new_strint(int64_max)
   total = a + b
   if (total%to_string(remove_0_padding=.true.) /= '-1') error stop 'opposite signs'
   print '(a)', 'Signed minimum plus signed maximum: -1'
   print '(a)', 'PASS strith'
end program demo_decimal_strings

gams_procedures.notes: Signed decimal-string integer addition and subtraction beyond 64-bit range, plus unsigned interpretation of an int64 bit pattern. This is fixed-capacity decimal representation, not unlimited arbitrary precision.

description: Linked lists and tree containers with insertion, searching and sorting operations.
source:
module integer_list_order
   use common_mod, only: DATA_KIND
   implicit none
contains
   integer function compare_values(a, b) result(order)
      integer(DATA_KIND), intent(in) :: a(:), b(:)
      order = 0
      if (a(1) < b(1)) order = -1
      if (a(1) > b(1)) order = 1
   end function compare_values
end module integer_list_order

program demo_linked_list
   use common_mod, only: DATA_KIND
   use dll_mod, only: dll_t
   use dllnode_mod, only: dllnode_t, dllnode_read
   use integer_list_order, only: compare_values
   implicit none
   type(dll_t) :: values
   type(dllnode_t), pointer :: node
   integer(DATA_KIND), parameter :: input(*) = [4_DATA_KIND, 1_DATA_KIND, 3_DATA_KIND, 2_DATA_KIND, 3_DATA_KIND]
   integer(DATA_KIND), parameter :: expected(*) = [1_DATA_KIND, 2_DATA_KIND, 3_DATA_KIND, 3_DATA_KIND, 4_DATA_KIND]
   integer(DATA_KIND), allocatable :: item(:)
   integer :: i

   do i = 1, size(input)
      call values%append([input(i)])
   end do
   if (values%count([3_DATA_KIND]) /= 2) error stop 'duplicate count'
   call values%sort(compare_values)
   node => values%firstnode()
   print '(a)', 'Sorted linked list:'
   do i = 1, size(expected)
      if (.not. associated(node)) error stop 'list too short'
      item = dllnode_read(node)
      if (size(item) /= 1) error stop 'node shape'
      if (item(1) /= expected(i)) error stop 'sort order'
      print '(i4)', item(1)
      node => node%nextnode()
   end do
   if (associated(node)) error stop 'list too long'
   node => values%index([2_DATA_KIND])
   if (.not. associated(node)) error stop 'search'
   call values%remove([2_DATA_KIND])
   if (values%count([2_DATA_KIND]) /= 0) error stop 'remove'
   if (values%count([3_DATA_KIND]) /= 2) error stop 'other entries changed'
   call values%clear()
   if (associated(values%firstnode())) error stop 'clear'
   print '(a)', 'PASS list'
end program demo_linked_list

description: Coulomb, Stribeck and dynamic friction models for contacting bodies.
source:
program demo_friction_curves
   use, intrinsic :: iso_fortran_env, only: real64
   use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   use friction, only: coulomb_model, stribeck_model
   implicit none
   type(coulomb_model) :: dry
   type(stribeck_model) :: sliding
   real(real64), parameter :: load = 20.0_real64
   real(real64), parameter :: velocities(*) = [-1.0_real64, -0.25_real64, 0.0_real64, 0.25_real64, 1.0_real64]
   real(real64) :: v, fc, fs, expected_c, expected_s, magnitude
   integer :: i

   ! Calling conventions follow the author's friction_model_tests.f90.
   dry%friction_coefficient = 0.3_real64
   sliding%static_friction_coefficient = 0.6_real64
   sliding%coulomb_friction_coefficient = 0.3_real64
   sliding%stribeck_velocity = 0.5_real64
   sliding%viscous_damping = 1.5_real64
   print '(a)', 'Velocity     Coulomb     Stribeck (N)'
   do i = 1, size(velocities)
      v = velocities(i)
      expected_c = 0.0_real64
      expected_s = 0.0_real64
      if (v /= 0.0_real64) then
         expected_c = sign(6.0_real64, v)
         magnitude = 6.0_real64 + 6.0_real64*exp(-4.0_real64*v*v)
         expected_s = sign(magnitude, v) + 1.5_real64*v
      end if
      fc = dry%evaluate(0.0_real64, 0.0_real64, v, load)
      fs = sliding%evaluate(0.0_real64, 0.0_real64, v, load)
      if (.not. ieee_is_finite(fc) .or. .not. ieee_is_finite(fs)) error stop 'nonfinite force'
      if (abs(fc - expected_c) > 1.e-12_real64) error stop 'Coulomb force'
      if (abs(fs - expected_s) > 1.e-12_real64) error stop 'Stribeck force'
      print '(3f12.6)', v, fc, fs
   end do
   if (dry%has_internal_state() .or. sliding%has_internal_state()) error stop 'unexpected internal state'
   print '(a)', 'The library reports signed friction; a force balance must use its chosen sign convention.'
   print '(a)', 'PASS friction'
end program demo_friction_curves

description: Evaluate mathematical expressions supplied as strings at scalar or array inputs.
source:
program demo_equation_parser
   use, intrinsic :: iso_fortran_env, only: real64
   use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   use FEQParse, only: EquationParser
   implicit none
   type(EquationParser) :: gaussian, polynomial
   real(real64) :: xyz(3), actual, expected, actual_poly, expected_poly
   integer :: i

   gaussian = EquationParser('f = exp(-(x^2 + y^2 + z^2))', ['x', 'y', 'z'])
   polynomial = EquationParser('g = (x + 2*y)^2 + z', ['x', 'y', 'z'])
   print '(a)', 'x          parsed Gaussian       direct Gaussian'
   do i = -3, 3
      xyz = [real(i, real64)/2.0_real64, 0.25_real64, -0.5_real64]
      actual = gaussian%evaluate(xyz)
      expected = exp(-sum(xyz**2))
      actual_poly = polynomial%evaluate(xyz)
      expected_poly = (xyz(1) + 2.0_real64*xyz(2))**2 + xyz(3)
      if (.not. ieee_is_finite(actual) .or. .not. ieee_is_finite(actual_poly)) error stop 'nonfinite evaluation'
      if (abs(actual - expected) > 1.e-12_real64) error stop 'Gaussian evaluation'
      if (abs(actual_poly - expected_poly) > 1.e-12_real64) error stop 'polynomial evaluation'
      print '(f6.2, 2f22.14)', xyz(1), actual, expected
   end do
   print '(a)', 'Polynomial precedence and multivariable evaluation also checked.'
   print '(a)', 'PASS feq-parse'
end program demo_equation_parser

program demo_dot_products
   use kinds, only: rk
   use fordot, only: dot_product
   use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   implicit none
   real(rk), parameter :: u(*) = [1.0_rk, 2.0_rk, 3.0_rk, 4.0_rk, 5.0_rk, 6.0_rk, 7.0_rk, 8.0_rk]
   real(rk), parameter :: v(*) = [8.0_rk, 7.0_rk, 6.0_rk, 5.0_rk, 4.0_rk, 3.0_rk, 2.0_rk, 1.0_rk]
   character(2), parameter :: methods(*) = ['m1', 'm2', 'm3', 'm4']
   real(rk) :: plain, blocked
   integer :: i

   print '(a)', 'Method      ordinary       three unequal blocks'
   do i = 1, size(methods)
      plain = dot_product(u, v, option=methods(i))
      blocked = dot_product(u, v, option=methods(i), nblock=3)
      if (.not. ieee_is_finite(plain) .or. .not. ieee_is_finite(blocked)) error stop 'nonfinite product'
      if (abs(plain - 120.0_rk) > 1.e-10_rk) error stop 'ordinary dot product'
      if (abs(blocked - 120.0_rk) > 1.e-10_rk) error stop 'blocked dot product'
      print '(a, 2f18.8)', methods(i), plain, blocked
   end do
   print '(a)', 'One process; these correctness checks are not a performance benchmark.'
   print '(a)', 'PASS fordot'
end program demo_dot_products

description: Matrix products with transpose options and selectable multiplication methods.
source:
program demo_matrix_products
   use kinds, only: rk
   use formatmul, only: matmul
   use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   implicit none
   character(2), parameter :: methods(*) = ['m1', 'm2', 'm3', 'm4']
   real(rk) :: a(2, 3), b(3, 2), expected(2, 2), c(2, 2), vector(3), product(2)
   integer :: i, j, k, method

   a = reshape([1.0_rk, 4.0_rk, 2.0_rk, 5.0_rk, 3.0_rk, 6.0_rk], shape(a))
   b = reshape([7.0_rk, 9.0_rk, 11.0_rk, 8.0_rk, 10.0_rk, 12.0_rk], shape(b))
   ! An independent scalar-loop reference, rather than this module's MATMUL.
   expected = 0.0_rk
   do j = 1, 2
      do i = 1, 2
         do k = 1, 3
            expected(i, j) = expected(i, j) + a(i, k)*b(k, j)
         end do
      end do
   end do
   vector = [1.0_rk, -2.0_rk, 3.0_rk]
   ! At this pinned version, pass BOTH transpose flags when specifying either.
   ! A single explicitly false flag incorrectly selects a transposed branch.
   do method = 1, size(methods)
      c = matmul(a, b, option=methods(method))
      call check(c)
      c = matmul(a, b, transA=.false., transB=.false., option=methods(method))
      call check(c)
      c = matmul(transpose(a), b, transA=.true., transB=.false., option=methods(method))
      call check(c)
      c = matmul(a, transpose(b), transA=.false., transB=.true., option=methods(method))
      call check(c)
      c = matmul(transpose(a), transpose(b), transA=.true., transB=.true., option=methods(method))
      call check(c)
      product = matmul(a, vector, option=methods(method))
      if (any(.not. ieee_is_finite(product))) error stop 'nonfinite vector product'
      if (maxval(abs(product - [6.0_rk, 12.0_rk])) > 1.e-10_rk) error stop 'matrix-vector product'
      print '(a)', methods(method)//': rectangular, transposed and matrix-vector products checked'
   end do
   print '(a)', 'A times B:'
   do i = 1, 2
      print '(2f12.3)', expected(i, :)
   end do
   print '(a)', 'PASS formatmul'
contains
   subroutine check(matrix)
      real(rk), intent(in) :: matrix(:, :)
      if (any(.not. ieee_is_finite(matrix))) error stop 'nonfinite matrix product'
      if (maxval(abs(matrix - expected)) > 1.e-10_rk) error stop 'matrix product'
   end subroutine check
end program demo_matrix_products

gams_procedures.notes: Methods m1 through m4 are checked for rectangular matrix multiplication, all transpose combinations and a matrix-vector product. The demo is single-process and does not validate every implementation or coarray branch. At this pin a single explicitly false transpose flag is misrouted; the demo passes both flags whenever either is specified. Separate failing probes and the successful workaround are retained.

description: Fixed-width binary-string arithmetic, shifts and logical operations.
source:
program demo_binary_strings
   use bstrith, only: add, sub, xor, not, shift_l, shift_r
   implicit none
   character(8) :: bits, expected
   integer :: i, amount

   ! Exhaustively check every eight-bit value, including carry and wraparound.
   do i = 0, 255
      write(bits, '(b8.8)') i
      write(expected, '(b8.8)') modulo(i + 1, 256)
      if (add(bits, '00000001') /= expected) error stop 'addition'
      if (sub(expected, '00000001') /= bits) error stop 'subtraction round trip'
      if (xor(bits, not(bits)) /= '11111111') error stop 'complement and xor'
      do amount = 1, 7
         write(expected, '(b8.8)') iand(ishft(i, amount), 255)
         if (shift_l(bits, amount) /= expected) error stop 'left shift'
         write(expected, '(b8.8)') ishft(i, -amount)
         if (shift_r(bits, amount) /= expected) error stop 'right shift'
      end do
   end do
   print '(a)', '11111111 + 00000001 = '//add('11111111', '00000001')
   print '(a)', '00000000 - 00000001 = '//sub('00000000', '00000001')
   print '(a)', 'Left shift 00010101 by 2: '//shift_l('00010101', 2)
   print '(a)', 'All 256 eight-bit values passed arithmetic, logical and shift checks.'
   print '(a)', 'PASS bstrith'
end program demo_binary_strings

gams_procedures.notes: Fixed-width binary-string addition, subtraction, shifts and logical operations. The driver checks every eight-bit value, including carry and wraparound. This is not unlimited arbitrary-precision arithmetic.

description: Finite-difference models of Fourier and Cattaneo heat transport.
source:
program demo_fourier_diffusion
   use constants, only: real12, int12, pi
   use globe_data, only: ra
   use solver, only: SRSin, linbcg
   use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   implicit none
   integer, parameter :: n = 31, steps = 50
   real(real12), parameter :: h = 1.0_real12/(n + 1), dt = 0.001_real12, r = dt/h**2
   real(real12) :: matrix(n, n), position(n), temperature(n), rhs(n), expected(n)
   real(real12) :: error, residual, discrete_factor, pde_error
   integer(int12) :: iterations
   integer :: i, step

   ! u_t = u_xx on [0,1], zero endpoint temperatures, u(x,0) = sin(pi*x).
   ! Use HeatFlow's sparse solver for backward-Euler steps of this independent
   ! one-dimensional discretization, rather than its full Cattaneo application.
   matrix = 0.0_real12
   do i = 1, n
      position(i) = i*h
      matrix(i, i) = 1.0_real12 + 2.0_real12*r
      if (i > 1) matrix(i, i - 1) = -r
      if (i < n) matrix(i, i + 1) = -r
   end do
   call SRSin(matrix, 0.0_real12, ra)
   temperature = sin(pi*position)
   do step = 1, steps
      rhs = temperature
      temperature = 0.0_real12
      iterations = 0_int12
      call linbcg(rhs, temperature, 1_int12, 1.e-11_real12, 100_int12, iterations, error)
      if (any(.not. ieee_is_finite(temperature))) error stop 'nonfinite temperature'
      residual = maxval(abs(matmul(matrix, temperature) - rhs))
      if (residual > 1.e-10_real12) error stop 'linear system residual'
   end do
   discrete_factor = (1.0_real12 + 4.0_real12*r*sin(pi*h/2.0_real12)**2)**(-steps)
   expected = discrete_factor*sin(pi*position)
   if (maxval(abs(temperature - expected)) > 1.e-9_real12) error stop 'discrete diffusion solution'
   expected = exp(-pi*pi*steps*dt)*sin(pi*position)
   pde_error = maxval(abs(temperature - expected))
   if (pde_error > 0.004_real12) error stop 'continuous solution accuracy'
   print '(a, f7.3)', 'Time: ', steps*dt
   print '(a, 2f14.9)', 'Midpoint numerical / analytical: ', temperature((n + 1)/2), expected((n + 1)/2)
   print '(a, es12.3)', 'Maximum error against the continuous heat equation: ', pde_error
   print '(a, es12.3)', 'Last independent linear-system residual: ', residual
   deallocate(ra%val, ra%irow, ra%jcol)
   print '(a)', 'PASS heatflow'
end program demo_fourier_diffusion

description: High-resolution WENO reconstruction and TVD integration for conservation equations.
source:
module advection_problem
   use hrweno_kinds, only: rk
   use hrweno_weno, only: weno
   implicit none
   integer, parameter :: n = 64
   real(rk), parameter :: dx = 1.0_rk/n
   type(weno) :: reconstruction
contains
   subroutine rhs(t, u, du)
      real(rk), intent(in) :: t, u(:)
      real(rk), intent(out) :: du(:)
      real(rk) :: extended(n+6), left(n+6), right(n+6), flux(0:n)
      ! Three periodic ghost cells at either end of the physical domain.
      extended(4:n+3) = u
      extended(1:3) = u(n-2:n)
      extended(n+4:n+6) = u(1:3)
      call reconstruction%reconstruct(extended, left, right)
      ! Unit positive advection speed: upwind flux is the right cell value.
      flux(0) = right(3)
      flux(1:n) = right(4:n+3)
      flux(n) = flux(0)
      du = -(flux(1:n)-flux(0:n-1))/dx
   end subroutine rhs
end module advection_problem

program periodic_advection
   use advection_problem
   use hrweno_tvdode, only: rktvd
   use ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   implicit none
   type(rktvd) :: solver
   real(rk), parameter :: pi = acos(-1.0_rk), dt = 0.002_rk
   real(rk) :: x(n), u(n), exact(n), time, factor, error, mass
   integer :: i
   x = [( (i-0.5_rk)*dx, i=1,n )]
   ! Exact cell averages, rather than point samples.
   factor = sin(pi*dx)/(pi*dx)
   u = 1 + 0.2_rk*factor*sin(2*pi*x)
   reconstruction = weno(ncells=n+6, k=3, eps=1.e-6_rk)
   solver = rktvd(rhs, n, order=3)
   time = 0
   call solver%integrate(u, time, 0.25_rk, dt)
   exact = 1 + 0.2_rk*factor*sin(2*pi*(x-time))
   error = maxval(abs(u-exact))
   mass = sum(u)*dx
   if (.not.all(ieee_is_finite(u))) error stop 'Nonfinite solution'
   if (abs(time-0.25_rk)>1.e-12_rk .or. error>1.e-4_rk) error stop 'Advection error'
   if (abs(mass-1.0_rk)>1.e-11_rk) error stop 'Mass conservation error'
   print '(a,f8.3)', 'Periodic advection time: ', time
   print '(a,es12.4)', 'Maximum cell-average error: ', error
   print '(a,f16.12)', 'Conserved mass: ', mass
   print *, 'PASS hrweno'
end program periodic_advection

gams_procedures.notes: WENO spatial reconstruction and explicit TVD Runge-Kutta integration for conservation equations. The main checks a smooth periodic advection problem against exact cell averages and verifies conservation of mass; discontinuous solutions and nonuniform grids are not covered.

description: Reduce the number of polyline points using geometric simplification algorithms.
source:
program simplify_curve
   ! This pin has upstream limitations in radial_distance and in repeated
   ! perpendicular_distance calls. This example makes one perpendicular call.
   ! Reproducers: docs/fpm-candidates/fortran-simplify in the playground repo.
   use iso_fortran_env, only: dp => real64
   use ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   use simplify, only: perpendicular_distance
   use pyplot_module, only: pyplot
   implicit none
   integer, parameter :: n=251
   real(dp), parameter :: pi=acos(-1.0_dp), tolerance=0.005_dp
   real(dp) :: curve(n,2), fraction, interpolated, max_error
   real(dp), allocatable :: reduced(:,:)
   type(pyplot) :: plot
   integer :: i, j, status
   curve(:,1) = [(2*pi*(i-1)/(n-1),i=1,n)]
   curve(:,2) = sin(curve(:,1))
   ! One pass of perpendicular-distance simplification.
   reduced = perpendicular_distance(curve, tolerance)
   if (.not.all(ieee_is_finite(reduced))) error stop 'Nonfinite coordinates'
   if (size(reduced,1)>=n .or. size(reduced,1)<2) error stop 'Unexpected point count'
   if (any(reduced(1,:)/=curve(1,:))) error stop 'First endpoint lost'
   if (any(reduced(size(reduced,1),:)/=curve(n,:))) error stop 'Last endpoint lost'
   max_error = 0
   j = 1
   do i=1,n
      do while (j<size(reduced,1)-1)
         if (curve(i,1)<=reduced(j+1,1)) exit
         j = j+1
      end do
      fraction = (curve(i,1)-reduced(j,1))/(reduced(j+1,1)-reduced(j,1))
      interpolated = (1-fraction)*reduced(j,2)+fraction*reduced(j+1,2)
      max_error = max(max_error,abs(curve(i,2)-interpolated))
   end do
   if (max_error>tolerance) error stop 'Independent interpolation check failed'
   print '(a,i0,a,i0)', 'Sine curve: ',n,' points reduced to ',size(reduced,1)
   print '(a,es12.4)', 'Maximum vertical interpolation error: ',max_error
   call plot%initialize(grid=.true.,legend=.true.,title='Polyline simplification', &
      xlabel='x',ylabel='sin(x)',use_oo_api=.true.)
   call plot%add_plot(curve(:,1),curve(:,2),label='Original',linestyle='b-')
   call plot%add_plot(reduced(:,1),reduced(:,2),label='Simplified',linestyle='r.')
   call plot%savefig('simplified.png',istat=status)
   if (status/=0) error stop 'Plot generation failed'
   print *, 'PASS fortran-simplify'
end program simplify_curve

gams_procedures.notes: Polyline simplification. The main checks one call of perpendicular-distance reduction against endpoints and an independent interpolation bound, and plots the original and reduced curves. Separate GNU 16 probes confirm incorrect radial-distance filtering and lost endpoints on consecutive perpendicular-distance calls at this pin; see the retained reproducers. The single-call example does not fix those upstream limitations.

program dense_inference
   use iso_fortran_env, only: real32
   use ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   use athena, only: full_layer_type, array_type
   implicit none
   type(full_layer_type) :: layer
   type(array_type) :: input(1,1)
   real(real32) :: weights(2,3), bias(2), x(3,1), reference(2)
   ! Deterministic inference: no data files, training loop or random weights.
   weights = reshape([1.,-1.,2.,0.5,-0.5,3.], [2,3])
   bias = [0.25_real32,-0.75_real32]
   x(:,1) = [1.,2.,-1.]
   layer = full_layer_type(num_inputs=3, num_outputs=2, activation='tanh')
   layer%params(1)%val(:,1) = reshape(weights,[6])
   layer%params(2)%val(:,1) = bias
   call input(1,1)%allocate(source=x)
   call layer%forward(input)
   reference = tanh(matmul(weights,x(:,1))+bias)
   if (.not.all(ieee_is_finite(layer%output(1,1)%val))) error stop 'Nonfinite output'
   if (maxval(abs(layer%output(1,1)%val(:,1)-reference))>2.e-6_real32) &
      error stop 'Dense layer does not match direct Fortran calculation'
   print '(a)', 'Fully connected layer: 3 inputs, 2 outputs, tanh activation'
   print '(a,2f12.7)', 'Athena inference: ', layer%output(1,1)%val(:,1)
   print '(a,2f12.7)', 'Direct reference: ', reference
   print *, 'PASS athena'
end program dense_inference

gams_procedures.notes: Neural-network function approximation. A fixed-weight dense layer with tanh activation is compared against direct Fortran matrix multiplication and TANH. This does not test training, automatic derivatives, graph convolutions or model accuracy on a dataset. K remains broad.

description: Arithmetic, logical and shift operators for stdlib-backed bitsets.
source:
program morton_neighbor
   use orbs
   implicit none
   type(operable_bitset) :: key, neighbor, one, mask_x, mask_y, expected
   character(4) :: text, expected_text
   integer :: code, x, y, next_x, next_code
   mask_x = operable_bitset('1010')
   mask_y = operable_bitset('0101')
   ! A 4-bit Morton key interleaves two bits of x with two bits of y.
   do code=0,15
      write(text,'(b4.4)') code
      key = operable_bitset(text)
      one = orbs_one(mold=key)
      neighbor = (((key.or.mask_y)+one).and.mask_x).or.(key.and.mask_y)
      ! Independent reference using ordinary integer bit operations.
      x = ibits(code,1,1) + 2*ibits(code,3,1)
      y = ibits(code,0,1) + 2*ibits(code,2,1)
      next_x = modulo(x+1,4)
      next_code = 2*ibits(next_x,0,1) + 8*ibits(next_x,1,1) &
         + ibits(y,0,1) + 4*ibits(y,1,1)
      write(expected_text,'(b4.4)') next_code
      expected = operable_bitset(expected_text)
      if (neighbor/=expected) error stop 'Morton neighbor mismatch'
      if (code==3) print '(a)', 'Morton key '//text//' -> x neighbor '//expected_text
   end do
   print '(a)', 'Verified all 16 cells, including periodic wraparound.'
   print *, 'PASS orbs'
end program morton_neighbor

gams_procedures.notes: Fixed-width bitset arithmetic and logical operations. The main computes an x neighbor for every cell of a two-dimensional 4-by-4 Morton grid, checking all sixteen results and wraparound against independent intrinsic integer operations.

description: Educational growable real arrays with spare capacity to reduce reallocations.
source:
program growable_matrix
   use iso_fortran_env, only: real64
   use rearrayfx, only: rearray_real64_r2
   implicit none
   integer :: i
   block
      type(rearray_real64_r2) :: matrix
      real(real64) :: expected(2,6)
      matrix%overprov = 2.0
      expected = reshape([(real(i,real64),i=1,12)], [2,6])
      call matrix%allocate([2,2])
      matrix%view = expected(:,1:2)
      ! This growth fits in the spare capacity; existing elements survive.
      call matrix%allocate([2,3])
      if (any(matrix%view(:,1:2)/=expected(:,1:2))) error stop 'First growth lost data'
      matrix%view(:,3) = expected(:,3)
      ! This growth needs a new backing allocation.
      call matrix%allocate([2,6])
      if (any(matrix%view(:,1:3)/=expected(:,1:3))) error stop 'Reallocation lost data'
      matrix%view(:,4:6) = expected(:,4:6)
      print '(a,2i4)', 'Final matrix shape: ', shape(matrix%view)
      print '(a,f8.1)', 'Sum of preserved and appended elements: ', sum(matrix%view)
      if (any(matrix%view/=expected)) error stop 'Matrix data mismatch'
      call matrix%allocate([2,1])
      if (any(matrix%view/=expected(:,1:1))) error stop 'Shrink lost data'
      matrix = expected(:,1:2)
      if (any(matrix%view/=expected(:,1:2))) error stop 'Array assignment failed'
   end block
   print *, 'PASS rearrayfx'
end program growable_matrix

gams_procedures.notes: Growable real rank-two arrays backed by spare capacity. The main checks data preservation across growth within spare capacity, reallocation, shrinking and plain-array assignment. This proof of concept is not a general-purpose container or a test of copying between container instances.

description: AMOS interfaces for complex-argument, noninteger-order Bessel and related functions.
source:
program complex_bessel_functions
   use iso_fortran_env, only: dp=>real64
   use ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   use amos, only: f90_zbesj, f90_zbesi, f90_zbesk
   implicit none
   complex(dp) :: z, j(1), modified_i(1), modified_k(1), reference_j, reference_i, reference_k
   real(dp), parameter :: nu=0.3_dp, pi=acos(-1.0_dp)
   integer :: underflows, status
   z=cmplx(1.0_dp,0.5_dp,dp)
   call f90_zbesj(z,nu,1,1,j,underflows,status)
   if(status/=0 .or. underflows/=0) error stop 'J calculation failed'
   call f90_zbesi(z,nu,1,1,modified_i,underflows,status)
   if(status/=0 .or. underflows/=0) error stop 'I calculation failed'
   call f90_zbesk(z,0.5_dp,1,1,modified_k,underflows,status)
   if(status/=0 .or. underflows/=0) error stop 'K calculation failed'
   reference_j=power_series(z,nu,-1)
   reference_i=power_series(z,nu,1)
   reference_k=sqrt(pi/(2*z))*exp(-z)
   if(.not.all(ieee_is_finite([real(j(1)),aimag(j(1)),real(modified_i(1)),aimag(modified_i(1)), &
      real(modified_k(1)),aimag(modified_k(1))]))) error stop 'Nonfinite result'
   if(abs(j(1)-reference_j)>1.e-11_dp) error stop 'J disagrees with independent series'
   if(abs(modified_i(1)-reference_i)>1.e-11_dp) error stop 'I disagrees with independent series'
   if(abs(modified_k(1)-reference_k)>1.e-11_dp) error stop 'K half-order identity failed'
   print '(a)', 'Complex argument z = 1 + 0.5i; noninteger orders'
   print '(a,2f18.12)', 'J_0.3(z), real/imag: ',real(j(1)),aimag(j(1))
   print '(a,2f18.12)', 'I_0.3(z), real/imag: ',real(modified_i(1)),aimag(modified_i(1))
   print '(a,2f18.12)', 'K_0.5(z), real/imag: ',real(modified_k(1)),aimag(modified_k(1))
   print *, 'PASS amosf90'
contains
   function power_series(x,order,sign_factor) result(value)
      complex(dp),intent(in)::x
      real(dp),intent(in)::order
      integer,intent(in)::sign_factor
      complex(dp)::value,term,total
      integer::k
      term=cmplx(1.0_dp,0.0_dp,dp);total=term
      do k=1,60
         term=term*(sign_factor*x*x/4)/(k*(order+k))
         total=total+term
         if(abs(term)<epsilon(1.0_dp)*abs(total)) exit
      end do
      value=(x/2)**order*total/gamma(order+1)
   end function power_series
end program complex_bessel_functions

gams_procedures.notes: AMOS module interfaces for complex-argument Bessel functions with noninteger nonnegative order, including modified Bessel functions. The checked main compares J_0.3 and I_0.3 at 1+0.5i with independent convergent power series and K_0.5 with its closed form. Other argument regions, orders, scaling modes and Airy/Hankel routines are not validated. The upstream README warns of possible bugs.

program checked_lapack_operations
   use iso_fortran_env, only: dp=>real64
   use ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   use linalg_fortran, only: linalg
   implicit none
   real(dp) :: a(3,3), inverse(3,3), vectors(3,3), eigenvalues(3), identity(3,3), determinant
   integer :: i
   a=reshape([2._dp,1._dp,0._dp,1._dp,2._dp,1._dp,0._dp,1._dp,2._dp],[3,3])
   identity=0
   do i=1,3
      identity(i,i)=1
   end do
   inverse=a
   if(.not.linalg%inv(inverse)) error stop 'Inverse failed'
   if(.not.all(ieee_is_finite(inverse))) error stop 'Nonfinite inverse'
   if(maxval(abs(matmul(a,inverse)-identity))>1.e-11_dp) error stop 'Inverse residual'
   determinant=linalg%det(a)
   if(abs(determinant-4._dp)>1.e-11_dp) error stop 'Determinant mismatch'
   vectors=a
   call linalg%eigh(vectors,eigenvalues)
   if(.not.all(ieee_is_finite(eigenvalues))) error stop 'Nonfinite eigenvalues'
   if(maxval(abs(eigenvalues-[2-sqrt(2._dp),2._dp,2+sqrt(2._dp)]))>1.e-11_dp) &
      error stop 'Eigenvalue mismatch'
   do i=1,3
      if(maxval(abs(matmul(a,vectors(:,i))-eigenvalues(i)*vectors(:,i)))>1.e-11_dp) &
         error stop 'Eigenpair residual'
   end do
   if(maxval(abs(matmul(transpose(vectors),vectors)-identity))>1.e-11_dp) &
      error stop 'Eigenvectors are not orthonormal'
   print '(a,f12.8)', 'Determinant: ',determinant
   print '(a,3f14.9)', 'Eigenvalues: ',eigenvalues
   print '(a,es12.4)', 'Inverse residual: ',maxval(abs(matmul(a,inverse)-identity))
   print *, 'PASS linalg_fortran'
end program checked_lapack_operations
