description: Growable integer vectors with insertion, removal and duplicate elimination.
source:
program editable_integer_vector
   use fortran_vector, only: vector_int,size
   implicit none
   type(vector_int)::values
   integer::i,last
   call values%init(2)
   do i=1,8
      call values%append(i)
   end do
   if(size(values)/=8) error stop 'Growth lost elements'
   do i=1,8
      if(values%get(i)/=i) error stop 'Growth changed an element'
   end do
   call values%append([3,1,9,9])
   call values%unique()
   if(size(values)/=9) error stop 'Duplicate removal failed'
   do i=1,9
      if(values%get(i)/=i) error stop 'Unique order was not preserved'
   end do
   call values%remove(4)
   call values%delete(2)
   last=values%pop()
   if(last/=9) error stop 'Wrong final element'
   if(size(values)/=6) error stop 'Wrong edited size'
   do i=1,6
      block
         integer,parameter::expected(6)=[1,3,5,6,7,8]
         if(values%get(i)/=expected(i)) error stop 'Wrong edited contents'
      end block
   end do
   call values%cut()
   print '(a)', 'After growth, unique, remove, delete and pop:'
   call values%write()
   call values%clear()
   print *, 'PASS fortran_vector'
end program editable_integer_vector

gams_procedures.notes: Growable integer vectors. The checked main verifies growth from a two-element capacity, appended arrays, stable duplicate removal, remove/delete/pop and final compaction against independent expected contents. A checksum-guarded one-line edit fixes aliasing in unique: remove the already saved first value instead of the first array element while that array is being compacted. Empty-vector unique and all invalid-input cases are not covered.

description: Character-by-character text scanning with bounded navigation for small parsers.
source:
program scan_configuration
   use scanner, only: textscanner
   use stdlib_string_type, only: string_type, assignment(=)
   implicit none
   type(textscanner)::scan
   type(string_type)::input
   character(*),parameter::record='steps=12;dt=0.25'
   character(len(record))::recovered
   integer::i,code,steps,separator,status
   real::dt
   input=record
   call scan%new(input)
   ! Reconstruct the complete record through the scanner API.
   do i=1,len(record)
      code=scan%current()
      if(code<0) error stop 'Unexpected end of text'
      recovered(i:i)=achar(code)
      if(i<len(record)) then
         code=scan%next()
         if(code<0) error stop 'Unexpected end while advancing'
      end if
   end do
   if(recovered/=record) error stop 'Text reconstruction mismatch'
   if(scan%next()/=-1) error stop 'Scanner advanced beyond the end'
   call scan%first()
   if(scan%prev()/=-1) error stop 'Scanner moved before the beginning'
   call scan%jump_to(iachar('='))
   if(scan%current()/=iachar('=')) error stop 'First equals not found'
   if(scan%peek()/=iachar('1')) error stop 'Peek mismatch'
   if(scan%current()/=iachar('=')) error stop 'Peek moved the cursor'
   separator=index(recovered,';')
   read(recovered(7:separator-1),*,iostat=status) steps
   if(status/=0) error stop 'Integer conversion failed'
   call scan%jump_to(iachar(';'))
   call scan%jump_to(iachar('='))
   if(scan%peek()/=iachar('0')) error stop 'Second field not found'
   read(recovered(separator+4:),*,iostat=status) dt
   if(status/=0) error stop 'Real conversion failed'
   if(steps/=12 .or. abs(dt-0.25)>epsilon(dt)) error stop 'Parsed values mismatch'
   print '(a)', 'Scanned: '//recovered
   print '(a,i0,a,f6.3)', 'steps=',steps,'  dt=',dt
   print '(a)', 'End boundaries and non-moving peek verified.'
   print *, 'PASS scanner'
end program scan_configuration

gams_procedures.notes: Character-by-character text scanning. The main reconstructs a configuration record through current/next, verifies navigation and end boundaries, and checks that peek does not move the cursor. The recovered fields are converted with ordinary internal READ and compared with known values; this is a small parser example, not a full parsing language.

description: Construct, parse and serialize JSON values with explicit error handling.
source:
program json_round_trip
   use rojff
   implicit none
   type(fallible_json_value_t) :: document, field, restored, invalid
   character(:),allocatable :: serialized
   document=parse_json_from_string('{"steps":12,"dt":0.25,"label":"heat"}')
   if(document%failed()) error stop 'JSON parsing failed'
   select type(object=>document%value_)
   type is(json_object_t)
      field=object%get('steps')
      if(field%failed()) error stop 'Missing steps'
      select type(value=>field%value_)
      type is(json_integer_t)
         if(value%number/=12) error stop 'Wrong integer value'
      type is(json_number_t)
         if(abs(value%number-12.d0)>1.d-12) error stop 'Wrong numeric value'
      class default
         error stop 'steps is not numeric'
      end select
      field=object%get('dt')
      if(field%failed()) error stop 'Missing dt'
      select type(value=>field%value_)
      type is(json_number_t)
         if(abs(value%number-0.25d0)>1.d-12) error stop 'Wrong dt'
      class default
         error stop 'dt is not a number'
      end select
      field=object%get('label')
      if(field%failed()) error stop 'Missing label'
      select type(value=>field%value_)
      type is(json_string_t)
         if(value%string/='heat') error stop 'Wrong label'
      class default
         error stop 'label is not a string'
      end select
      field=object%get('absent')
      if(.not.field%failed()) error stop 'Missing-key error was not reported'
   class default
      error stop 'Expected a JSON object'
   end select
   serialized=document%value_%to_compact_string()
   restored=parse_json_from_string(serialized)
   if(restored%failed()) error stop 'Round-trip parsing failed'
   if(restored%value_%to_compact_string()/=serialized) error stop 'Round trip changed data'
   invalid=parse_json_from_string('{"dt": }')
   if(.not.invalid%failed()) error stop 'Invalid JSON was accepted'
   print '(a)', 'Round-trip JSON: '//serialized
   print '(a)', 'Values, missing-key reporting and malformed-input reporting verified.'
   print *, 'PASS rojff'
end program json_round_trip

gams_procedures.notes: JSON parsing and serialization with explicit error values. The main checks numeric/string fields, missing-key reporting, compact serialization round trips and malformed-input rejection. It uses the original Erloff 2.2.0 API with a pinned compatible Strff 3.1.1 and ISO varying string 3.0.3; the Strff 4.0 dependency graph needs an unavailable GitHub mirror. No computational source is patched.

description: Object-oriented parsing of typed command-line options, defaults and named arguments.
source:
program typed_command_line
   use iso_fortran_env, only: dp=>real64
   use argparse, only: argparser
   implicit none
   type(argparser)::arguments
   character(2048)::executable
   integer::command_status,exit_status,length,status
   ! The playground starts a main without arguments. Relaunch this executable
   ! once with a fixed example command line to exercise the real parser API.
   if(command_argument_count()==0) then
      call get_command_argument(0,executable,length=length,status=status)
      if(status/=0 .or. length>len(executable)) error stop 'Cannot obtain executable path'
      call execute_command_line('"'//trim(executable)//'" -t 4 --scale 0.25 --name demo --verbose', &
         exitstat=exit_status,cmdstat=command_status)
      if(command_status/=0 .or. exit_status/=0) error stop 'Example command line failed'
   else
      arguments=argparser('Checked scientific command-line options')
      call arguments%set_program_name('example')
      call arguments%add_option_integer('-t','--threads','Thread count',1)
      call arguments%add_option_double('-s','--scale','Scale factor',1.0_dp)
      call arguments%add_option_string('-n','--name','Run label','unnamed')
      call arguments%add_option_integer('-i','--iterations','Iteration count',20)
      call arguments%add_option_logical('-v','--verbose','Enable verbose output')
      call arguments%parse()
      if(arguments%get_option_integer('--threads')/=4) error stop 'Integer option mismatch'
      if(abs(arguments%get_option_double('--scale')-0.25_dp)>1.e-12_dp) error stop 'Real option mismatch'
      if(trim(arguments%get_option_string('--name'))/='demo') error stop 'String option mismatch'
      if(arguments%get_option_integer('--iterations')/=20) error stop 'Default option mismatch'
      if(.not.arguments%has_option('--verbose')) error stop 'Logical option mismatch'

program unsigned_boundaries
   use iso_fortran_env, only: int64
   use unsigned_m
   use int_m, only: int
   implicit none
   type(uint32)::a,b,result
   type(uint16)::small
   integer(int64),parameter::modulus=4294967296_int64
   integer(int64)::expected
   a=2147483648_int64
   b=3
   result=a+b
   expected=2147483651_int64
   if(int(result)/=expected) error stop 'Addition across signed boundary failed'
   if(.not.(a>b)) error stop 'Unsigned comparison failed'
   print '(a,i0)', '2147483648 + 3 = ',int(result)
   a=modulus-1
   b=1
   result=a+b
   if(int(result)/=0_int64) error stop '32-bit addition did not wrap'
   result=b-a
   if(int(result)/=2_int64) error stop '32-bit subtraction did not wrap'
   a=-10
   if(int(a)/=modulus-10) error stop 'Negative assignment conversion failed'
   small=65535
   if(int(small)/=65535) error stop '16-bit upper boundary failed'
   small=small+1
   if(int(small)/=0) error stop '16-bit addition did not wrap'
   print '(a)', 'Verified 16/32-bit boundaries, wraparound and negative assignment.'
   print *, 'PASS uint-fortran'
end program unsigned_boundaries

module numerical_specification
   use veggies, only: result_t,assert_equals
   implicit none
contains
   pure double precision function simpson(values,h) result(integral)
      double precision,intent(in)::values(3),h
      integral=h*(values(1)+4*values(2)+values(3))/3
   end function simpson
   function constant_case() result(check)
      type(result_t)::check
      check=assert_equals(6.d0,simpson([3.d0,3.d0,3.d0],1.d0))
   end function constant_case
   function linear_case() result(check)
      type(result_t)::check
      check=assert_equals(2.d0,simpson([0.d0,1.d0,2.d0],1.d0))
   end function linear_case
   function quadratic_case() result(check)
      type(result_t)::check
      check=assert_equals(8.d0/3,simpson([0.d0,1.d0,4.d0],1.d0))
   end function quadratic_case
end module numerical_specification

program run_specification
   use numerical_specification
   use veggies, only: test_item_t,describe,it,run_tests
   implicit none
   type(test_item_t)::tests
   tests=describe('Simpson integration on [0,2]',[ &
      it('integrates a constant exactly',constant_case), &
      it('integrates a linear function exactly',linear_case), &
      it('integrates a quadratic exactly',quadratic_case)])
   if(.not.run_tests(tests)) error stop 'Numerical specification failed'
   print *, 'PASS veggies'
end program run_specification

gams_procedures.notes: Functional unit-testing framework. The main runs three specification-style cases checking a small user-written Simpson formula against known constant, linear and quadratic integrals. The numerical formula belongs to the example, not the package. Parallel testing, generators and the complete framework are not validated.

module arithmetic_callbacks
   use parser_module, only: parser_t,token_t
   implicit none
contains
   function operand(self,token) result(answer)
      class(parser_t)::self
      type(token_t)::token,answer
      real::value
      integer::status
      read(token%string,*,iostat=status) value
      if(status/=0) error stop 'Invalid numeric operand'
      answer%object=value
   end function operand
   function unary(self,operation,argument) result(answer)
      class(parser_t)::self
      type(token_t)::operation,argument,answer
      select type(value=>argument%object)
      type is(real)
         select case(operation%string)
         case('-');answer%object=-value
         case('+');answer%object=value
         case('sqrt');answer%object=sqrt(value)
         case default;error stop 'Unsupported unary operation'
         end select
      class default
         error stop 'Wrong unary operand type'
      end select
   end function unary
   function binary(self,left,operation,right) result(answer)
      class(parser_t)::self
      type(token_t)::left,operation,right,answer
      select type(a=>left%object)
      type is(real)
         select type(b=>right%object)
         type is(real)
            select case(operation%string)
            case('+');answer%object=a+b
            case('-');answer%object=a-b
            case('*');answer%object=a*b
            case('/');answer%object=a/b
            case('^');answer%object=a**b
            case default;error stop 'Unsupported binary operation'
            end select
         class default
            error stop 'Wrong right operand type'
         end select
      class default
         error stop 'Wrong left operand type'
      end select
   end function binary
end module arithmetic_callbacks

program checked_expressions
   use arithmetic_callbacks
   use ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   implicit none
   type(parser_t)::parser
   type(token_t)::result
   character(24),parameter::expressions(5)=[character(24):: &
      '2+3*4','(2+3)*4','2^3^2','sqrt(9)','-2+6']
   real,parameter::expected(5)=[14.,20.,512.,3.,4.]
   integer::i
   call parser%register_unary(['-   ','+   '])
   call parser%register_function(['sqrt'])
   call parser%register_operator(['^   '],is_right_assoc=.true.)
   call parser%register_operator(['+   ','-   ','*   ','/   '])
   call parser%ignore_tokens([' '])
   parser%on_operand=>operand
   parser%on_unary=>unary
   parser%on_binary=>binary
   do i=1,size(expressions)
      result=parser%parse(trim(expressions(i)))
      select type(value=>result%object)
      type is(real)
         if(.not.ieee_is_finite(value)) error stop 'Nonfinite expression value'
         if(abs(value-expected(i))>1.e-5) error stop 'Expression mismatch'
         print '(a,a,f10.3)',trim(expressions(i)),' = ',value
      class default
         error stop 'Wrong result type'
      end select
   end do
   print *, 'PASS shunting-yard-fortran'
end program checked_expressions

gams_procedures.notes: Token-based expression parsing with user-supplied callbacks. The main checks precedence, parentheses, right-associative exponentiation, square root and unary minus against five exact results. The author documents global registrations, fixed precedences and missing syntax validation; concurrent parsers and malformed expressions are not supported by this example.

program main

   implicit none
   type(SqliteDatabase_t) :: db
   type(SqliteStatement_t) :: query
   type(varying_string) :: message, remaining
   double precision :: average
   call check(sqliteff_open(':memory:', db), SQLITE_OK)
   call check(sqliteff_exec(db, 'create table measurements(value real);' // &
      'insert into measurements values(2.0),(4.0),(6.0);', message), SQLITE_OK)
   call check(sqliteff_prepare(db, 'select count(*), avg(value) from measurements;', &
      query, remaining), SQLITE_OK)
   call check(sqliteff_step(query), SQLITE_ROW)
   if (sqliteff_column_int(query, 0) /= 3) error stop 'row count'
   average = sqliteff_column_double(query, 1)
   if (abs(average - 4.0d0) > 1.0d-12) error stop 'average'
   print '(a,f5.2)', 'Average of three measurements: ', average
   call check(sqliteff_step(query), SQLITE_DONE)
   call check(sqliteff_finalize(query), SQLITE_OK)
   call check(sqliteff_close(db), SQLITE_OK)
   print *, 'PASS sqliteff'
contains
   subroutine check(actual, expected)
      integer, intent(in) :: actual, expected
      if (actual /= expected) then
         print *, 'Unexpected SQLite status:', actual, ' expected:', expected
         error stop 'SQLite operation failed'
      end if
   end subroutine
end program

program main
   use iso_c_binding, only: c_int32_t, c_int64_t
   use integer32_set, only: int32_set, new_int32_set
   use integer64_set, only: int64_set, new_int64_set
   implicit none
   type(int32_set) :: small
   type(int64_set) :: large

   do i = 5, 1, -1
      call small%push(int(i, c_int32_t))

   print *, 'Unique sorted values after removing 2:', small%data

   if (large%size /= 1) error stop '64-bit duplicate'
   if (large%data(1) /= 5000000000_c_int64_t) error stop '64-bit value'

! Adapted from the author's user_object_smart_pointer example.
module demo_resource
   use smart_pointer_m, only: sp_smart_pointer_t
   implicit none
   integer :: cleanup_count = 0
   type, extends(sp_smart_pointer_t) :: resource_t
      integer, pointer :: value => null()
   contains
      procedure :: free
   end type
contains
   impure elemental subroutine free(self)
      class(resource_t), intent(inout) :: self
      if (associated(self%value)) then
         deallocate(self%value)
         nullify(self%value)
         cleanup_count = cleanup_count + 1
      end if
   end subroutine
end module

program main
   use demo_resource
   implicit none
   call exercise()
   if (cleanup_count /= 1) error stop 'cleanup count'
   print *, 'Resource cleaned up exactly once'
   print *, 'PASS smart-pointers'
contains
   subroutine exercise()
      type(resource_t) :: first, second
      allocate(first%value, source=42)
      call first%start_counter()
      if (first%reference_count() /= 1) error stop 'initial count'
      second = first
      if (first%reference_count() /= 2) error stop 'shared count'
      if (.not. associated(first%value, second%value)) error stop 'shared resource'
      if (second%value /= 42) error stop 'resource value'
      print *, 'Shared value:', second%value, 'references:', first%reference_count()
      if (cleanup_count /= 0) error stop 'premature cleanup'
   end subroutine
end program

gams_procedures.notes: Reference-counted resource management. Adapted from the author example: a user type extends sp_smart_pointer_t and implements free. The checked main shares one integer resource, verifies reference counts and shared target, checks no premature cleanup and confirms exactly one cleanup after subroutine return. No source edits. This is not exhaustive compiler finalization conformance testing.

program main

   use nc4fortran, only: netcdf_file
   implicit none
   type(netcdf_file) :: file
   real(real64) :: original(2,3), restored(2,3)
   character(32) :: units
   integer :: unit
   original = reshape([1.0_real64, 2.0_real64, 3.0_real64, &
      4.0_real64, 5.0_real64, 6.0_real64], [2,3])
   call file%open('measurements.nc', action='w')
   call file%write('temperature', original, ['x','y'])
   call file%write_attribute('temperature', 'units', 'kelvin')
   call file%close()
   call file%open('measurements.nc', action='r')
   call file%read('temperature', restored)
   call file%read_attribute('temperature', 'units', units)
   call file%close()
   if (any(abs(restored-original) > 1.0e-12_real64)) error stop 'array round trip'

end program

program main

   implicit none

         total = total+values(i,j)

program main
   use iso_fortran_env, only: real64
   use mpmodule
   use playground_kronrod, only: init, kronrod, nwds2
   implicit none
   integer, parameter :: n = 3
   type(mp_real) :: nodes(n+1), weights(n+1), gauss(n+1), tolerance, integral, expected
   real(real64) :: result
   integer :: power, i
   if (mpipl < 1000) error stop 'Kronrod requires MPFUN configured for at least 1000 digits'
   call init()
   tolerance = mpreal(10.0_real64, nwds2)**(-40)
   call kronrod(n, tolerance, nodes, weights, gauss)
   ! The routine returns only the nonnegative half of the symmetric 7-point rule.
   do power = 0, 10, 2
      integral = mpreal(0.0_real64, nwds2)
      do i = 1, n
         integral = integral+2*weights(i)*nodes(i)**power
      end do
      if (power == 0) integral = integral+weights(n+1)
      expected = mpreal(2.0_real64, nwds2)/(power+1)
      if (abs(integral-expected) > tolerance) error stop 'polynomial integral'
      result = dble(integral)
      print '(a,i0,a,f18.14)', 'Integral of x^', power, ' on [-1,1]: ', result
   end do
   print *, 'PASS kronrod'
end program

description: FIFO queue using C storage for fixed-size values.
source:
program main
   use iso_c_binding, only: c_int64_t, c_sizeof, c_ptr, c_f_pointer, c_associated
   use fifo_queue, only: fifo, new_fifo_queue
   implicit none
   type(fifo) :: queue
   ! An 8-byte payload also keeps the following C pointer header aligned here.
   integer(c_int64_t), target :: input
   integer(c_int64_t), pointer :: output
   type(c_ptr) :: memory
   integer :: i
   interface
      subroutine c_free(pointer) bind(C, name='free')
         import c_ptr
         type(c_ptr), value :: pointer
      end subroutine
   end interface
   queue = new_fifo_queue(c_sizeof(input))
   do i = 1, 4
      input = 10*i
      call queue%push(input)
   end do
   if (queue%count() /= 4) error stop 'initial count'
   do i = 1, 4
      if (.not. queue%pop(memory)) error stop 'early empty queue'
      if (.not. c_associated(memory)) error stop 'null item'
      call c_f_pointer(memory, output)
      if (output /= 10*i) error stop 'FIFO order'
      print *, 'Popped:', output
      ! Items were allocated by C; release them with C free.
      call c_free(memory)
      nullify(output)
   end do
   if (.not. queue%is_empty()) error stop 'not empty'
   if (queue%count() /= 0) error stop 'final count'
   if (queue%pop(memory)) error stop 'extra item'
   call queue%destroy()
   print *, 'PASS for_fifo_queue'
end program

gams_procedures.notes: FIFO container using C allocations and byte copies. The main enqueues four 64-bit C-interoperable integers, verifies count and exact retrieval order, frees every popped allocation with C free, checks empty-pop behavior and destroys the queue. No source edits. The implementation uses GNU LOC and raw byte storage; the example makes no portability claim for arbitrary derived types, pointer-owning values, threading or every compiler.

program main

   if (re_match('^temp=\d+\.\d+$', 'temp=warm')) error stop 'negative match'
   number = trim(re_match_str('\d+\.\d+', 'temp=23.50 kelvin'))

   call re_split('\s*,\s*', 'red, green,blue', fields)

   if (any(fields /= [character(8) :: 'red','green','blue'])) error stop 'split fields'

   print '(a)', 'Matched number: '//number
   print '(a)', 'Fields: '//trim(fields(1))//', '//trim(fields(2))//', '//trim(fields(3))

source:
program main
   use iso_fortran_env, only: real64
   use ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   use fortime, only: timer
   implicit none
   type(timer) :: wall, cpu
   integer :: i
   real(real64) :: total, expected

   call wall%timer_start()
   call cpu%ctimer_start()
   total = 0.0_real64
   do i = 1, 100000
      total = total + real(i, real64)
   end do
   call cpu%ctimer_stop(message='CPU seconds:')
   call wall%timer_stop(message='Wall seconds:')
   expected = 100000.0_real64 * 100001.0_real64 / 2
   if (total /= expected) error stop 'sum'
   if (.not. ieee_is_finite(wall%elapsed_time)) error stop 'wall time'
   if (.not. ieee_is_finite(cpu%cpu_time)) error stop 'CPU time'
   if (wall%elapsed_time < 0 .or. cpu%cpu_time < 0) error stop 'negative time'
   print '(a,f16.0)', 'Sum of integers 1 through 100000: ', total
   print '(a)', 'Timings illustrate the API; shared sandbox timings vary.'
   print '(a)', 'PASS fortime'
end program main

description: Extensible assertions for scalar and array values and numerical tolerances.
source:
program main
   use iso_fortran_env, only: real64
   use fassert, only: assert_equal, assert_approx_equal, expect_equal
   implicit none
   logical :: passed
   character(:), allocatable :: message

   call assert_equal(2 + 3, 5, 'integer addition')
   call assert_equal([1, 4, 9], [1, 4, 9], 'integer array')
   call assert_approx_equal(sqrt(2.0_real64)**2, 2.0_real64, 'square root round trip', &
      tolerance=1.0e-12_real64)
   ! Capture an intentional failure so the program can inspect it and continue.
   call expect_equal(2 + 3, 6, 'intentional mismatch', passed, output_message=message)
   if (passed) error stop 'mismatch not detected'
   if (index(message, 'intentional mismatch') == 0) error stop 'missing diagnostic'
   print '(a)', 'Scalar, array and approximate comparisons passed.'
   print '(a)', 'Captured expected failure:'
   print '(a)', message
   print '(a)', 'PASS fassert'
end program main

gams_procedures.notes: Assertions for integer scalars and arrays plus approximate real comparison with an explicit tolerance. The main captures an intentional failed comparison as a logical status and message, checks both, and continues successfully. No source edits; matches the existing Any dependency revision. Not a validation of every type, rank, tolerance convention, custom comparator or test-framework integration.

description: Return and inspect structured error statuses and messages.
source:
program main
   use iso_fortran_env, only: real64
   use errstat, only: error_stat_type, catch_error, set_success, error_occurred
   implicit none
   type(error_stat_type) :: status
   real(real64) :: value

   value = reciprocal(4.0_real64, status)
   if (error_occurred(status)) error stop 'unexpected error'
   if (value /= 0.25_real64) error stop 'reciprocal'
   print '(a,f6.2)', '1 / 4 = ', value
   value = reciprocal(0.0_real64, status)
   if (.not. error_occurred(status)) error stop 'zero not rejected'
   if (status%get_status() /= 1) error stop 'error code'
   if (status%get_message() /= 'Cannot divide by zero') error stop 'error message'
   print '(a,i0,2a)', 'Status ', status%get_status(), ': ', status%get_message()
   value = reciprocal(2.0_real64, status)
   if (error_occurred(status)) error stop 'error not cleared'
   if (value /= 0.5_real64) error stop 'recovery'
   print '(a)', 'A subsequent valid call clears the error.'
   print '(a)', 'PASS errstat'
contains
   function reciprocal(x, status) result(y)
      real(real64), intent(in) :: x
      type(error_stat_type), intent(out) :: status
      real(real64) :: y
      y = 0
      if (x == 0) then
         call catch_error(1, 'Cannot divide by zero', status)
         return
      end if
      y = 1 / x
      call set_success(status)
   end function reciprocal
end program main

gams_procedures.notes: Error status and message handling. A custom reciprocal routine uses catch_error and set_success. The main checks a successful result, zero rejection with an exact code and message, and a subsequent successful call clearing the error. No source edits. The reciprocal is only a driver, not a mathematical procedure supplied by errstat. Optional omitted-status termination and user-defined task/message repositories are not exercised.

description: Generic singly linked list with reusable storage for small datasets.
source:
program main
   use sll_module, only: sll, iterator, sll_finalizer, iterator_finalizer
   implicit none
   type(sll) :: list
   type(iterator) :: iter
   class(*), pointer :: item
   integer :: n, capacity

   call list%push_back(7)
   call list%push_back(2.5)
   if (list%size() /= 2) error stop 'list size'
   capacity = list%size(.true.)
   iter = iterator(list)
   n = 0
   do while (iter%next(item))
      n = n + 1
      select type (item)
      type is (integer)
         if (n /= 1 .or. item /= 7) error stop 'integer element'
         print '(a,i0)', 'Integer: ', item
      type is (real)
         if (n /= 2 .or. item /= 2.5) error stop 'real element'
         print '(a,f4.1)', 'Real: ', item
      class default
         error stop 'unexpected type'
      end select
   end do
   if (n /= 2) error stop 'iteration count'
   call iterator_finalizer(iter)
   call list%empty()
   if (.not. list%is_empty()) error stop 'empty'
   call list%push_back(9)
   if (list%size() /= 1) error stop 'reused size'
   if (list%size(.true.) /= capacity) error stop 'capacity changed'
   iter = iterator(list)
   if (.not. iter%next(item)) error stop 'missing reused element'
   select type (item)
   type is (integer)
      if (item /= 9) error stop 'reused value'
   class default
      error stop 'reused type'
   end select
   print '(a,i0)', 'Capacity retained after emptying and reusing: ', capacity
   call iterator_finalizer(iter)
   call sll_finalizer(list)
   print '(a)', 'PASS slinked-list'
end program main

gams_procedures.notes: Generic singly linked list for small datasets. The main checks integer and real payloads in insertion order, list size, iteration count, emptying, retained capacity and the value stored after reuse; iterator and list cleanup are explicit. A checksum-guarded compatibility edit removes PURE from node_init, whose result has a polymorphic allocatable component. Constructor allocation and copying are unchanged, and the call sites are impure. This patched root retains its own small archive instead of sharing an unmodified graph export. No display dependency is needed for the custom consumer. Large-data performance, all mutation operations and ownership of pointer-containing derived types are not validated.
